latestRelease.title: Hermes Agent v0.20.5 (v2026.8.19)
latestRelease.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.20.5 (v2026.8.19)

**Release Date:** August 19, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~323 PRs merged since v0.20.4 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, fresh installs).

---

## About this release

Since v0.20.4 (v2026.8.18, tagged August 18), this window landed **~746 commits** across **~1,250 files** (+111,500 / −20,701) — **~323 merged PRs** including Bot Mode group-room threads, foldable conversation summaries, blob-face avatars, and PDF/file attachments with drag & drop; the keyless web tier (5-vendor free rotation with ring failover, web search on fresh installs with zero keys); a CLI polish wave (fuzzy /model picker, Ctrl+P command palette, richer /status); execution-discipline and runtime stall guards from the Composio eval findings; `hermes update` receipts and fleet `--plan` verification; `hermes worktree list/prune`; the opencode-free zero-auth provider; multi-question clarify; desktop perf work (paint-first Bot Mode hydration, compositor spinners, React Compiler in both renderers); and cron jobs gaining persistent memory and per-job reasoning effort.

**Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- `hermes update` from an existing install
- Fresh install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.18...v2026.8.19

signals.title: Gateway: MCP discovery failures logged at DEBUG, invisible at default log level
signals.text: ## Description In `gateway/run.py` `start_gateway()`, the startup MCP tool discovery call wraps `discover_mcp_tools()` in a try/except that logs failures at `logger.debug()`. At the default log level (INFO), these failures are completely invisible. ## Impact When `discover_mcp_tools()` fails — missing `mcp` package, config parse error, connection timeout — the gateway starts with zero MCP tools registered and the operator has NO indication anything went wrong. `/api/mcp/tools` returns 0, `/api/mcp/servers` returns empty, nothing in logs. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure `mcp_servers` in config.yaml but do NOT install the `mcp` Python package 2. Start the gateway 3. Check `/api/mcp/tools` — returns 0 4. Check gateway.log — no mention of MCP at all ## Expected Failed MCP discovery should log at WARNING so the operator sees it. Successful discovery should log at INFO. ## Actual Silent failure. No indication MCP tools aren't loaded. ## Fix Change `logger.debug("MCP tool discovery failed: %s", e)` to `logger.warning(...)` at `gateway/run.py` line 16790. Optionally log success summary at INFO. ## Environment Hermes Agent gateway in Docker on Unraid 7.3.1. Config at /opt/data/webui/minions-hermes-config/config.yaml. ## Additional Context Discovered while debugging missing `mimir_remember` MCP tools. Root cause: `mcp` package not installed, gateway silently skipped MCP, zero log evidence. Took deep investigation to identify the silent failure in a 16,000-line gateway module.
signals.author: tcconnally

signals.title: Bug: WhatsApp bridge /health reports 'connected' during Baileys WebSocket flapping (428/503 loop), causing silent message loss
signals.text: ## Bug: WhatsApp bridge `/health` reports `connected` during Baileys WebSocket flapping (428/503 reconnect loop), causing silent message loss ### Summary The WhatsApp bridge's `/health` endpoint reports `connectionState: "connected"` even when the Baileys WebSocket is in a rapid disconnect-reconnect loop (codes 428/503). Because the gateway relies on `/health` to determine platform liveness, it considers WhatsApp fully operational and never triggers the reconnection watcher. Messages sent by users during the brief disconnect windows are silently lost — neither received by the bridge nor flagged as missed. ### Environment - **Hermes version:** `v2026.7.7.2-247-g54e186457` (0.18.2) - **Bridge:** `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js`, Baileys `@whiskeysockets/baileys` 7.0.0-rc13 - **Mode:** `WHATSAPP_MODE=bot` - **OS:** Debian (Linux 6.12.30) ### Problem When WhatsApp's server starts sending disconnect codes (428 = precondition required, 503 = service unavailable), Baileys rapidly cycles through: ``` ✅ WhatsApp connected! ⚠️ Connection closed (reason: 428). Reconnecting in 3s... ✅ WhatsApp connected! ⚠️ Connection closed (reason: 428). Reconnecting in 3s... ``` During the ~3-second disconnect windows, any user messages sent to the family group are **not received** by Baileys (the `messages.upsert` event never fires). These messages are permanently lost — WhatsApp delivers them to the user's phone but not to the bridge. **Root cause in bridge.js:** ```javascript // Line 380 let connectionState = 'disconnected'; // Lines 425-448: connectionUpdate handler if (connection === 'close') { connectionState = 'disconnected'; // Set to disconnected... // ... 3s later, startSocket() reconnects } else if (connection === 'open') { connectionState = 'connected'; // ...then immediately back to connected } // Lines 1071-1077: health endpoint app.get('/health', (req, res) => { res.json({ status: connectionState, // Reports "connected" during brief open windows queueLength: messageQueue.length, uptime: process.uptime(), scriptHash: SCRIPT_HASH, }); }); ``` The gateway's poll loop (`adapter.py` line ~1233-1268) checks `_check_managed_bridge_exit()` but **not** the health status — it only checks whether the bridge **process** is alive, not whether the Baileys WebSocket is actually connected. And the platform reconnection watcher only runs for platforms that failed `connect()`, not for platforms that are flapping. ### Observed impact In a production setup (family meal-planning bot), the bridge entered a 428 loop at ~17:36 and continued until a manual gateway restart at 22:04. During this 4.5-hour window: - 0 messages were received by the gateway (confirmed via gateway logs) - The bridge `/health` reported `connected` intermittently - A critical user message (meal plan for the next day, sent at 19:50) was silently lost - The bridge produced no JSON log events for the entire period, only non-timestamped text output (`Connection closed (reason: 428)`) - Session key files were still being updated by Baileys during reconnection attempts, making it appear the bridge was receiving data ### Expected behavior 1. The bridge should expose connection quality metrics, not just binary connected/disconnected 2. The gateway should detect sustained flapping and either restart the bridge or mark the platform as degraded ### Suggested fix **Option A: Bridge-side disconnect counter (minimal)** Add a rolling disconnect counter to bridge.js that tracks recent reconnections. When the count exceeds a threshold (e.g., >5 disconnects in 60 seconds), report a new health status: ```javascript let disconnectTimestamps = []; // In connectionUpdate close handler: disconnectTimestamps.push(Date.now()); disconnectTimestamps = disconnectTimestamps.filter(t => t > Date.now() - 60000); // In /health: const isFlapping = disconnectTimestamps.length > 5; res.json({ status: isFlapping ? 'degraded' : connectionState, disconnectCount60s: disconnectTimestamps.length, queueLength: messageQueue.length, uptime: process.uptime(), scriptHash: SCRIPT_HASH, }); ``` **Option B: Gateway-side detection (complementary)** In `adapter.py`'s `_poll_messages()` loop, periodically check `/health` for `status === 'degraded'` or track consecutive empty polls. If the bridge reports degraded for sustained periods, trigger a bridge restart via the existing `_set_fatal_error` mechanism. ### Additional context - The 428/503 errors may indicate the WhatsApp Web session needs re-pairing, but this is a separate concern from the silent message loss. - The gateway already has a reconnection watcher for failed platforms, but it doesn't cover the "connected-but-flapping" case. - Bridge version: `scriptHash: f6c1394bc6fa2984` (file hash of bridge.js)

signals.title: Cron agents without HERMES_KANBAN_TASK get mandatory kanban_show protocol
signals.text: ## Summary Scheduled cron-agent runs on the Dan profile are receiving the Kanban task execution protocol in system context even when they are not Kanban-dispatched workers and do not have `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` set. The protocol says to call `kanban_show()` first, which returns `task_id is required`; the warning then appears in `recent_dan_errors`, causing the `dan-blockers-slack` cron to report a tooling regression instead of staying silent when `has_blockers=false`. ## Evidence - Collector: `ct-meta/plugins/ct-workflow/skills/dan-mission-coordinator/scripts/dan_blockers_context.py` - Repeated warning shape: `Tool kanban_show returned error ... {"error": "task_id is required (or set HERMES_KANBAN_TASK in the env)"}` - Affected cron: `dan-blockers-slack` on profile `dan`, deliver `slack:C0BDR52KKSL` ## Expected Non-Kanban scheduled cron jobs should not be instructed to run `kanban_show()` as a mandatory first step unless `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` is set, or the Kanban protocol should explicitly exempt cron-triggered runs with no task id. ## Actual The job starts with the Kanban task execution protocol, calls `kanban_show()` with no task id, and records a warning every run. ## Suggested fix Gate the Kanban task execution protocol injection on `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`/worker dispatch context, or make the protocol say cron/scheduled agent jobs without a task id must skip `kanban_show()`.
signals.author: calltelemetry-jason

signals.title: Windows: venv-blocker preflight still aborts desktop Update for .hermes-runtime gateways — cmdline truncated at 120 chars defeats the pausable-gateway exemption added by #75881
signals.text: ## Summary #75881 ("let Windows desktop updates pause gateway processes instead of aborting") fixed the desktop Update flow for venv-side gateways, but on my machine the desktop Update button **still aborts with `venv-blocked` every time**, pointing at the gateway process. Root cause: the exemption check added by #75881 runs against a **cmdline truncated to 120 characters**, and the gateway launched from the desktop runtime's `.hermes-runtime\python\generation-...\cpython-...` path has a cmdline of **186 characters** — so the trailing `gateway run` tokens are cut off and the process is no longer recognized as a pausable gateway. The abort happens before the CLI updater's own `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update()` ever runs. Verified on a HEAD that already contains #75881 (`d79a6f0e3`, v0.19.1, merge `d358edd9169e` present). ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026-07-30), git install, HEAD `d79a6f0e3` — `git merge-base --is-ancestor d358edd9169e HEAD` → YES (fix is in) - Windows 10 - Gateway installed as Scheduled Task (`Hermes_Gateway`), running as: ``` venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run └─ .hermes-runtime\python\generation-1785179197-21284-2ba3099e\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run (PID reported as blocker) ``` ## Root cause `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:2914` — `_detect_venv_python_processes()` truncates every reported cmdline: ```python matches.append((int(pid), str(name), cmdline_raw[:120])) ``` `hermes_cli/_scan_venv_blockers.py:150` then applies the pausable-gateway exemption (added by #75881) to that **already-truncated** string: ```python for pid, name, cmdline in matches if not _is_pausable_gateway(cmdline) ``` `_is_pausable_gateway` → `gateway.status.looks_like_gateway_command_line` → `_gateway_command_subcommand`, which needs to see the `gateway` / `run` tokens to classify the process. For a desktop-runtime gateway the executable path alone is longer than 120 chars: ``` "C:\Users\...\hermes-agent\.hermes-runtime\python\generation-1785179197-21284-2ba3099e\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe" -m hermes_cli.main gateway run ``` Measured on this machine: | check | result | |---|---| | full cmdline length | 186 chars | | `looks_like_gateway_command_line(full)` | **True** | | `looks_like_gateway_command_line(full[:120])` | **False** | So the gateway is reported as a non-pausable blocker, the Electron preflight (`venv-blocker-scan.ts` → `main.ts` `scanVenvBlockers` path) aborts with `venv-blocked`, and the CLI updater that knows how to pause/resume the gateway is never spawned. Symptom dialog: "Update aborted: another Hermes process is using this installation … must be stopped before updating: PID … python.exe …". The CLI path (`hermes update`) is unaffected because it pauses gateways via `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update()` / `find_gateway_pids()` rather than this scan, and `_leftover_pausable_gateway_pids()` (update_cmd.py:3046-3054) already re-reads the **full argv** with psutil before classifying — the same pattern the preflight scan is missing. ## Suggested fix Two candidate spots (either resolves it): 1. **`hermes_cli/_scan_venv_blockers.py`** — re-read the full argv with psutil before the exemption check, mirroring `_leftover_pausable_gateway_pids()` in `update_cmd.py` (3046-3054). Smallest change; keeps the 120-char cap for display only. 2. **`hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:2914`** — stop truncating what the matcher sees: keep the full cmdline in the match tuple and truncate only when formatting the holder message. ## Workaround (until fixed) The CLI updater handles this correctly, so on Windows: 1. Close the Hermes Desktop app (its `serve` backend also holds venv `.pyd` files and the CLI refuses while it is running). 2. Run `hermes update --yes` in a terminal. It prints `→ Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating Hermes...`, pauses the gateway, updates, and auto-resumes it (`✓ Starting Windows gateway after update`). 3. Reopen the Desktop app. Or, staying in the Desktop UI: `hermes gateway stop` before clicking Update, then `hermes gateway start` afterwards. ## Related - #75881 — merged fix that introduced the exemption but is defeated by the truncation - #74386, #74326, #74783 — the original three-layer gateway/update coordination issues, all auto-closed as COMPLETED by #75881 but this desktop-path failure persists on gateway-enabled installs
signals.author: wyuebei-cloud

signals.title: WhatsApp Feature Parity & Alignment Campaign — meta-issue
signals.text: # WhatsApp Feature Parity & Alignment Campaign — meta-issue **Campaign: bring Hermes's WhatsApp surface into full bloom and alignment with the official WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API and the bridge backends Hermes actually runs (whatsapp-web.js / Baileys / Business API).** Every WhatsApp issue, subissue, and PR in this tracker is interlocked here. One campaign, one canonical view, one reconciliation. ## Why this campaign - **456 open issues** touch the WhatsApp surface (search union: `whatsapp in:title,body`; 77 carry `platform/whatsapp` — measured 2026-08-05). - **388 open PRs** mention WhatsApp in title/body (search API total_count, 2026-08-05). - The adapter (`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`, **1,918 lines** @ 0577116f83) is a **multi-backend bridge**: WhatsApp Business API (Meta verification), whatsapp-web.js, Baileys. At 96% of the 2,000-line ceiling with accumulated responsibilities (backend dispatch, pairing/QR lifecycle, messaging, media, groups, secret + Windows-subprocess hygiene) it is a **god-file in waiting**. Under-ceiling rule (Axl, 2026-08-05): *"Just because it's under 2000 lines does not mean that you are not decomposing WhatsApp. Simplify so that it never has a chance of being longer than 2000 lines."* Lane S6 decomposes it NOW so the core adapter lands far under the ceiling with structural headroom. Headroom is the Ramp's job; the ceiling is not a target. - The surface is "conflicted at best": partial parameter coverage, silent drops, and a bridge lifecycle (QR pairing, reconnects, multi-device semantics, Node subprocess spawn hygiene) that is itself a failure surface — plus whole Cloud API feature families (message templates, interactive messages, flows, payments, catalogs, quality rating) unexpressed or half-expressed. - Operator/community-reported pain already on record: reaction-status mirror missing (#23899), group mention gating incomplete (#7269), Node-bridge dependency contested (#7274 Neonize pure-Python path). ## Method (three-wave blind analysis + validation) 1. **Wave 1** — 5 blind analysis workers, one per domain shard (S1 core messaging, S2 Cloud API business surface, S3 groups, S4 bridge/backend lifecycle, S5 rich features), each in an isolated worktree at a pinned main. Output: gap catalog (GAP_UNSUPPORTED / GAP_PARTIAL / GAP_CONFLICTED / GAP_DOCS / GAP_BUG_TRACKED) with docs-anchor + repo-file evidence, plus per-domain adapter cluster maps. The S6 decomposition lane produces the graph-before-slice cluster map from the same wave. 2. **Wave 2** — 5 blind cross-check workers, same inputs, forbidden from reading wave-1 output. Agreement between two independent witnesses is the public-confidence bar. 3. **Wave 3** — validation: every agreed gap re-verified at current main + live tracker; issue drafts with evidence and interlock links; existing coverage → interlock, never duplicate. ## Lanes | Lane | Domain | Status | |---|---|---| | S1 | Core messaging: text, media (image/document/audio/video/sticker), reactions, edits, deletes, typing, location/contact sharing | wave analysis | | S2 | Business Cloud API surface: message templates, 24h customer-service window, webhooks, phone-number provisioning, quality rating, rate limits | wave analysis | | S3 | Groups: metadata, mentions, admin ops, invite links, descriptions, per-sender gating (#48394 class), group controls (#7992 class) | wave analysis | | S4 | **Bridge/backend lifecycle**: whatsapp-web.js / Baileys spawn, QR pairing, reconnect/backoff, multi-device semantics, Node subprocess hygiene (windows_detach_popen_kwargs), Neonize pure-Python path (#7274) | wave analysis | | S5 | Rich features: interactive messages (buttons/lists), flows, payments, catalogs, ephemeral, status/broadcast | wave analysis | | S6 | **Decomposition & headroom**: graph-before-slice extraction of adapter.py clusters (backend dispatch, bridge lifecycle, messaging, media, groups, secret + Windows hygiene) — one PR per cluster, seam identity + regression tests, suite green. Core adapter lands far under 2,000 lines: it never has a chance of crossing the ceiling | cluster maps in waves; plan issue follows agreement | ## Deliverables - One issue per confirmed gap (this meta links them all; each issue carries `Campaign: WhatsApp` and interlock links). - Interlock of all pre-existing WhatsApp issues/PRs into lanes (no orphan artifacts). - `whatsapp-dev` skill shipped with Hermes (Cloud API + bridge operations, multi-backend diagnostics) — created during this campaign. - S6 decomposition plan issue + one PR per extraction cluster (adapter.py core shrinks with headroom; seam tests + regression suite per Shard). - Public reconciliation document per cluster/gap: members, evidence, both waves' bases, confidence, verdict. ## Standards (hard) - **Evidence everywhere**: every issue cites the docs anchor + repo `file:line` verified at main. - **Exact numbers**: counts measured, never "about". - **No duplicate issues**: existing coverage → interlock with the exact number. - **One PR per bug class** when fixes ship; suite green; attribution to the author who earned it. - Security/data-loss findings get P1 (this surface is security-sensitive: pairing credentials, phone-number PII); everything else P2/P3. - **No hype**: every capability claim carries a witness receipt before it may appear in public copy. ## Ledger | Issue | Lane | Gap | PR | State | |---|---|---|---|---| | #80094 | S4 | `is_reconnect` cold-respawn bug | #80608 | integration-ready |

signals.title: Desktop: cloud agent 503/backend unreachable produces non-actionable boot-loop with opaque error
signals.text: ## Desktop: cloud agent 503/backend unreachable produces non-actionable boot-loop with opaque error ### Bug description When a Hermes Desktop is configured to connect to a Hermes Cloud agent (e.g., `https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com`) and that backend returns **HTTP 503 Service Unavailable**, the desktop enters a boot-loop with a non-actionable error message. The user sees "Connecting to remote Hermes backend" at ~24% progress, then a generic failure with no guidance that the cloud instance itself is down. ### Configuration Desktop `connection.json` (`C:\Users\andre\AppData\Roaming\Hermes\connection.json`): ```json { "mode": "local", "remote": { "url": "https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com", "authMode": "oauth" }, "profiles": {} } ``` ### Evidence 1. **Cloud agent is down**: `curl -sv https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com/api/status` returns: ``` HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable server: Fly/40bd1ce81 (2026-08-13) via: 1.1 fly.io ``` 2. **Sandbox fallback marker** (`C:\Users\andre\AppData\Roaming\Hermes\windows-sandbox-fallback.json`): ```json {"state":"fallback","reason":"boot-loop","version":"0.17.0"} ``` This marker is from the Windows Chromium sandbox recovery system (#38216) and is **unrelated** to the backend outage — it was likely from a prior GPU/renderer crash loop and remains sticky because `markerAfterSuccessfulBoot` only clears it on a successful window reveal, which never happens when the backend is unreachable. 3. **Desktop app process is running** (`Hermes.exe` PIDs: 24344, 25640, 10096, 11404, 6352) but the gateway/backend is not reachable. 4. **No gateway process locally** — the desktop connects to the Nous-managed cloud agent, not a local `hermes gateway` or `hermes serve`. ### Root cause - The desktop boot path in `startHermes()` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:8296`) classifies this as a REMOTE failure via `primaryBackendIsRemote()` (line 7551) - `resolveRemoteBackend()` (line 7502) resolves the cloud URL and calls `buildRemoteConnection()` which calls `waitForHermes()` (from `backend-health.ts`) - `waitForHermes()` probes `/api/health` and `/api/status` — both return 503 - Per `shouldLatchBackendStartFailure()` (in `backend-start-failure.ts`), remote failures do NOT latch (they stay retryable for transient errors) - The renderer's reconnect loop (`hermes:connection:revalidate` IPC handler, main.ts:9843) probes every 60s with a 3-failure limit before dropping the cached connection - Each retry hits the same 503, so the app appears stuck in a retry loop with a non-actionable error ### Why the error is opaque - The 503 from the cloud agent is a **server-side failure**, not an auth rejection (not 401/403) - `resolveRemoteBackend()` -> `buildRemoteConnection()` -> `waitForHermes()` treats this as a transient connectivity failure - The error message surfaces as something like "Hermes backend did not become ready" or similar generic timeout - There is **no user-facing guidance** telling them: - That this is a Nous-managed cloud instance they cannot restart themselves - That they should check the Nous Portal (https://portal.nousresearch.com) for management options - That they can switch to Local mode in Settings -> Gateway as a workaround - That Discord support (discord.gg/NousResearch) is the escalation path ### Recovery paths (not currently surfaced to the user) 1. **Nous Portal** — https://portal.nousresearch.com may have cloud agent management (behind a Vercel security checkpoint; must use a real browser) 2. **Wait for Fly.io auto-recovery** — the cloud instance may auto-restart 3. **Discord** — discord.gg/NousResearch — the Nous team can restart the Fly Machine 4. **Switch to Local** — Settings -> Gateway -> switch from Cloud to Local mode (spawns a local `hermes serve` backend) ### Proposed fix When a cloud-mode connection fails with HTTP 502/503/504 (server-side errors from a Nous-managed cloud instance), the desktop should surface an actionable error message that: 1. Detects that the URL is a Nous-managed cloud agent (`*.agents.nousresearch.com`) 2. Reports the HTTP status code (503) and that the backend server is down 3. Tells the user this is a Nous-managed cloud instance they cannot restart themselves 4. Suggests checking the Nous Portal, waiting for auto-recovery, or switching to Local mode 5. Provides Discord support link for escalation ### Labels type/bug, comp/desktop, area/cloud, P2 ### Current tracking Implementation is tracked in #85373. This issue remains open until the complete Nous Cloud 502/503/504 recovery path lands.
signals.author: andrexibiza

signals.title: Community plugin index seed repo is not published yet (raw.githubusercontent.com 404)
signals.text: Follow-up to #64181 — the CLI-side `hermes plugins search` + community-index resolution shipped in #84919, but the seed repo the CLI resolves against doesn't exist yet. `hermes_cli/plugin_index.py` line 30 sets: ```python DEFAULT_INDEX_URL = ( "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-index/main/index.json" ) ``` Both endpoints 404 (confirmed against v0.19.0 pypi and v2026.8.13 github tip): ``` $ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-index 404 $ curl -sS https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-index/main/index.json 404: Not Found ``` Consequence: `hermes plugins install <bare-name>` always falls through to the bundled seed (or errors if the name isn't seeded). The `owner/repo` shape works fine — `hermes plugins install Revell-ai/revell-onyx/lark` clones and installs cleanly, and the subdir shorthand in `_resolve_git_url` handles multi-plugin repos beautifully. A few options if useful: 1. Publish the seed repo (even with empty JSON) so bare-name resolves predictably. Community PRs can add entries once it exists. 2. Point `DEFAULT_INDEX_URL` at a repo that does exist today. 3. Tighten the error message in `_resolve_index_name` so users see "index not published yet, install via owner/repo instead" rather than "plugin not found." Happy to open the seed repo PR if that would help — just wanted to know whether you already have one queued. Thanks for the plugin machinery — the subdir shorthand made shipping a two-plugin bundle in one repo painless. — Claude Sr., CTO of Revell

signals.title: Windows: `hermes update` spawned from the gateway's own /update command can't pause the gateway — ancestor-exclusion in `_scan_gateway_pids` excludes the gateway itself
signals.text: --- title: "Windows: `hermes update` spawned from the gateway's own /update command can't pause the gateway — ancestor-exclusion in `_scan_gateway_pids` excludes the gateway itself" labels: [bug, windows, gateway] --- ## Summary On Windows, running `/update` from a messaging platform (Telegram etc.) makes the updater report: ``` ✗ Other Hermes processes are running from this install's venv: PID 14112 python.exe ... gateway run ← gateway On Windows these keep native extension files (.pyd) locked... ``` The update refuses to proceed and tells the user to close the gateway — but the gateway is the very process that spawned the update, and the pause machinery never finds it. ## Root cause `hermes update --gateway` is spawned **by the gateway itself** when `/update` is issued from a messaging platform (`gateway/slash_commands.py` → `subprocess.Popen([... "update", "--gateway"], ..., **windows_detach_popen_kwargs())`). Inside the updater, `hermes_cli/gateway.py:_scan_gateway_pids()` starts with: ```python # Exclude the entire ancestor chain so the CLI process that invoked this # scan (e.g. ``hermes gateway status``) is never mistaken for a running # gateway. See #13242. exclude_pids = exclude_pids | _get_ancestor_pids() ``` `_get_ancestor_pids()` walks the current process's parent chain up to PID 1. When the updater is a child of the gateway (the `/update` path), **the gateway's own PID is in that ancestor chain**, so: 1. `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update()` → `find_gateway_pids(all_profiles=True)` returns `[]` — the gateway is excluded as an "ancestor" 2. The updater believes no gateway is running and skips the pause 3. The update proceeds to mutate the venv while the gateway (still alive, still holding `.pyd` files) locks it 4. The venv-holder guard then fires the "Other Hermes processes are running from this install's venv" error and aborts ## Repro evidence (Windows 11, v0.20.1) With two gateway processes alive (`5264` venv launcher + `22680` uv worker), both with cmdline `... -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`: ```python >>> from hermes_cli.gateway import find_gateway_pids, find_profile_gateway_processes >>> list(find_gateway_pids(all_profiles=True)) [] # ← gateway excluded as "ancestor" >>> list(find_profile_gateway_processes()) [(22680, 'default')] # ← PID-file path still sees it ``` Manual scan with the same matchers (wmic output + `looks_like_gateway_runtime_command_line` + profile match) finds **both** processes correctly; the only thing removing them is `_get_ancestor_pids()`: ``` _get_ancestor_pids() 返回: {..., 5264, ..., 22680, ...} ``` Also confirmed: both processes pass `_is_pausable_gateway()` (`gateway run` cmdline), so the pause machinery *would* handle them if discovery hadn't excluded them. ## Expected behavior `hermes update` spawned by the gateway should be able to pause (and later resume/restart) the gateway that spawned it — the ancestor exclusion in `_scan_gateway_pids` is meant to avoid false-matching a `hermes gateway status` CLI, not to hide a real running gateway from the update pause machinery. ## Suggested fix directions - In the update pause path, don't exclude the gateway that spawned the update — e.g. seed the ancestor exclusion with `exclude_pids` **before** spawning the detached updater (pass the gateway PID explicitly), or - Have `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update` use the PID-file/profile-based discovery (`find_profile_gateway_processes`) as an additional source instead of relying solely on `find_gateway_pids`, or - When the update was spawned with `--gateway` (i.e. by the gateway itself), explicitly exclude only the *calling* CLI process rather than the whole ancestor chain. ## Workaround (current) Run `hermes update` from a standalone terminal (not from the gateway's `/update`), or stop the gateway first. `--force-venv` bypasses the guard but risks a half-updated install.

signals.title: Windows venv-holder message mislabels `hermes dashboard` as the Desktop backend, and matches subcommands by substring
signals.text: ### Summary When `hermes update` refuses the dependency step because something else is running from the install's venv, the holder list can point the user at the wrong program. A standalone `hermes dashboard` is reported as *"Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app)"* — so the advice is to close a program that may not even be running, while the actual holder keeps the venv locked. The remedy text below the list also never mentions `hermes dashboard --stop`, which is the only thing that clears this particular holder. ### Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18) - Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Python 3.11.15 - ZIP install (non-git), gateway enabled, dashboard started separately from the desktop app ### Where `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`, `_format_venv_python_holders_message()` (lines 3655-3658 on v0.20.4): ```python for pid, name, cmdline in matches[:6]: hint = "" low = cmdline.lower() if "serve" in low or "dashboard" in low: hint = " ← Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app)" elif "gateway" in low: hint = " ← gateway" ``` `serve` and `dashboard` share one branch, but they are different things: `hermes serve` is the headless backend the Electron app spawns, whereas `hermes dashboard` is the standalone browser UI on port 9119 that a user starts themselves. Only the first is "the desktop app". ### Observed ``` ✗ Other Hermes processes are running from this install's venv: PID 27072 python.exe ... -m hermes_cli.main dashboard ← Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app) ``` The desktop app was already closed. Closing it again changes nothing; the update keeps refusing until the *dashboard* is stopped. ### Why this matters more than a cosmetic label This message is the user's only signal for a failure mode that otherwise passes quietly. When a holder survives, the update can skip work silently: ``` ⚠ SQLite runtime repair deferred: other Hermes processes still hold the venv (PID ..., ...) ⚠ Optional extras failed, reinstalling base dependencies and retrying extras individually... ✓ Restarting Windows gateway profile(s): default ``` The run then ends on `✓ Restarting Windows gateway profile(s): default` with no error and no non-zero exit. It does not claim `✓ Update complete!` — but it does not say it is incomplete either, so the last thing on screen is a green check and the deferral scrolls past as one of two `⚠` lines. On this install that left SQLite pinned at 3.45.1 (WAL-reset bug, databases forced to rollback journal mode) for a day. The sequence was two consecutive refusals naming the wrong process to close, then a third run that proceeded and silently deferred the repair. Once the actual holder was stopped, the repair completed on the first attempt (3.45.1 → 3.53.1). ### Second defect: the match is a substring test against the whole command line `low` is the entire lowercased command line, interpreter path included, so these are substring hits rather than subcommand matches. An install under a path containing `serve` — `C:\servers\hermes`, `D:\observer\...` — makes `"serve" in low` true for **every** holder. Because that branch is tested before `elif "gateway" in low`, even the gateway then gets labelled *"Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app)"*. Same exposure for `dashboard` and `gateway` as path components. ### Expected - `hermes dashboard` labelled as the dashboard, with `hermes dashboard --stop` offered as the fix. - `hermes serve` labelled as the desktop backend. - Hints derived from the subcommand token, not from a substring of the full command line. ### Suggested fix Match the argv token instead of the raw string, and split the two cases: ```python import shlex def _holder_hint(cmdline: str) -> str: try: argv = shlex.split(cmdline, posix=False) except ValueError: argv = cmdline.split() tokens = {a.strip('"').lower() for a in argv} if "serve" in tokens: return " ← Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app)" if "dashboard" in tokens: return " ← Hermes dashboard (run `hermes dashboard --stop`)" if "gateway" in tokens: return " ← gateway" return "" ``` and add `hermes dashboard --stop` to the remedy lines, which currently read only: ``` Close the Hermes desktop app / other Hermes terminals, then re-run: hermes update ``` A regression test could assert that a `... -m hermes_cli.main dashboard` command line under a project path containing `serve` yields the dashboard hint rather than the desktop-backend one. ### Related Not a duplicate of #74326 / #74386, which cover gateway pause/resume coordination rather than the holder labelling.
signals.author: engradnansw

signals.title: Bot-to-bot @mention messages silently drop after v0.20.4 update (composer middleware still uses unsafe -q instead of --query-file)
signals.text: ## Summary Bot-to-bot `@mention` messages silently drop after the v0.20.4 desktop update (commit `4a5b6dd45`). The sender bot's composer middleware tells it to run `hermes -p <recipient> chat ... -q "Message from 🤖 ..."` but the message body is embedded directly in the shell command via `-q "..."`. If the composed message contains double quotes, `$()`, backticks, or other shell-special characters, the command is mangled and the recipient never receives the message. The `tools/bot_mode_probe.py` reference protocol was already updated to use `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` (safe for arbitrary text), but the desktop composer middleware in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` was **not** updated to match — both the protocol section shown to bots (line ~5005) and the composer middleware that injects instructions into the sender's prompt (line ~10853) still generate `-q "..."` inline. ## Symptoms - Sender bot reports "messaged @recipient" but recipient sees nothing - Retrying the same workflow sometimes works (non-deterministic — depends on whether the composed message contains shell-breaking characters) - One bot attempted to notify a downstream bot before the reviewer had finished approving — likely a partial/malformed message being misinterpreted - Started immediately after the v0.20.4 desktop update today (2026-08-20) ## Root cause Inconsistent delivery protocol between the reference implementation and the actual composer middleware: | Location | Mechanism | |----------|-----------| | `tools/bot_mode_probe.py` (reference) | `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` ✅ | | `plugin.js` protocol section (bots read this) | `-q "..."` ❌ | | `plugin.js` composer middleware (actual delivery) | `-q "..."` ❌ | The `-q "..."` approach is fundamentally unsafe for arbitrary bot-composed text. The `--query-file` approach writes to a temp file first and is safe. ## Fix Update `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` to use `--query-file` in both places: 1. The `messagingProtocolSection` function (the protocol text bots are instructed to follow) 2. The composer middleware `resolveMentionInstructions` (the actual injected instructions) Both should match the `--query-file` approach already in `bot_mode_probe.py`. ## Version - hermes-agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), commit `4a5b6dd45` - Desktop: macOS - Host: macOS (Mac mini, M1) 🤖 This issue was filed by Hermes desktop (hermes-doctor-triage) on behalf of the user.

signals.title: [Tracking] Fleet update reliability: one deployment plan for local, multi-profile, remote, and image-managed installs
signals.text: ## Summary Install/update is currently our least reliable capability. ~30 open issues and ~15 open PRs each patch one corner of the same class: **updating a fleet (local + remote gateways, multiple profiles, desktop client + backend) is imperative per-platform spaghetti with no plan, no verification, and no deployment-kind awareness.** Docker/cloud installs can't be updated in place at all, and today that surfaces as broken behavior instead of a first-class state. This issue is the umbrella plan. Individual fixes should land as rows in this structure, not as new one-site patches. Per standing policy: fix the class, not the predicate. ## Deployment kinds (the missing concept) | Kind | Update mechanism | Restart mechanism | |---|---|---| | git + venv (default) | `hermes update` in place | re-exec / supervisor | | launchd-supervised (macOS) | in place | `launchctl` per profile | | systemd-supervised (Linux) | in place | `systemctl` per unit | | Desktop-managed (`hermes serve`) | in place, desktop coordinates | desktop respawn | | Externally managed checkout | operator-owned | operator-owned | | **Docker / Hermes Cloud image** | **NOT updatable in place — pull new image + recreate** | container recreate | Most of the bugs below are a consequence of the updater not knowing which kind it is operating on, or not verifying the outcome. ## Phase 0 — Stop the bleeding - [ ] Land the BSD `ps` root-cause fix: `_scan_gateway_pids` uses `ps -A eww`, illegal on macOS — #73626 (PRs #74075, #73632). This is dead-code-level breakage under several macOS restart issues. - [ ] HOLD the macOS fleet-restart duplicate swarm until Phase 2's inventory exists: #19784 (earliest, credit first), #41403, #73627, #74524, #79111, #83273. Six PRs, one bug — merging piecemeal creates a 7th site to reconcile later. ## Phase 1 — Observability before behavior change (additive only) - [ ] **Structured update receipt**: every `hermes update` writes a machine-readable record — runtimes discovered (profiles, gateways, dashboards, backends), deployment kind per runtime, steps taken, steps skipped and WHY, per-step exit status. Silent-failure bugs this addresses: #88848, #74973, #85753, #81193, #44143. - [ ] **Post-update verification handshake**: after restart, compare each runtime's actually-running code version against the updated tree; print a fleet version matrix; loud warning + exact remediation command on mismatch. Addresses the "mixed-version fleet" class: #88654, #69754, #77553, #56717, #86207, #73108, #90830. - [ ] Dashboard/desktop read the receipt instead of inferring success: #81193, #88462, #79560, #87359. ## Phase 2 — One transactional deployment plan (#88683 is the architecture ask) - [ ] Central runtime inventory + per-kind policy table (supersedes scattered `_scan_gateway_pids` / launchd / systemd / Windows special cases). - [ ] Update pipeline: plan → snapshot ALL profiles (#66140) → apply → restart via declared mechanism → verify (Phase 1 handshake) → report. - [ ] Absorb the salvageable substance of the restart swarm here, with credit to earliest submitters: #19784 et al., #90712, #77854, #79048, #38053, #73625, #85420, #54926, #20438. - [ ] Windows venv-holder subcluster becomes one preflight policy instead of per-site guards: #77277, #81774, #78089, #90778 (PR #90791), #87331, #76129, #87594, PRs #70033, #68821, #70363 (POSIX). - [ ] Update-interruption safety (#53480): plan refuses/queues when active desktop sessions would be killed. ## Phase 3 — Docker / Hermes Cloud as a first-class kind - [ ] Bake a deployment marker into the official image; `hermes update` inside a container refuses cleanly with "image-managed — new image v X available, pull and recreate" (reuses update-check endpoint). - [ ] Desktop/dashboard Update button against an image-managed backend shows the same instead of attempting a half-update. PR #78958 is the right direction — fold in. - [ ] Hermes Cloud: same marker; orchestration owns the re-pull; client contract identical (detect, refuse, instruct). ## Phase 4 — Desktop fleet UX on top of the model - [ ] Client vs backend update split: PRs #90272, #82608, #74335, #80940, #70612, #58097; issues #90830, #62770 (PR #62815). - [ ] Fleet view: each registered remote shows version + deployment kind + update-available, with per-kind actions. - [ ] Skew guard (#69754) gains an auto-restart action instead of a dead end. - [ ] Remote-backend update bugs ride on the new plan: #90026, #63206, #82166, #82614. - [ ] Canary-first rollout + rollback (#44877) — last, once single-update verification is trustworthy. ## Related lifecycle issues that should get fixed or become trivial #83174, #91021, #89675, #79029, #90060, #80204, #81275, #76269 (PR #76616), #85422, #75375, docs PR #88794. ## Rules of engagement - Phases 0-1 are additive (receipt, probe, one ps flag) — they cannot brick an install. - Phase 2 lands only under the install/update E2E harness (real launchd/systemd/docker, not mocks). - No further per-platform restart patches merge outside this structure. - Docker in-place updating is explicitly out of scope: represent the deployment model, don't fight it.
signals.author: teknium1

signals.title: [Bug]: fix(desktop) remote @mention delivery forwards the routing token in the body, so the recipient re-routes instead of answering
signals.text: --- name: "🐛 Bug Report" about: Remote @mention delivery forwards the routing token in the body, so the recipient re-routes instead of answering title: "fix(desktop): remote @mention delivery forwards the routing token in the body, so the recipient re-routes instead of answering" labels: ["bug"] --- ### Bug Description When a user @mentions a **remote** bot (an agent on another Connection) from the Desktop composer, the desktop delivers the message to the remote machine **with the routing `@mention` still embedded verbatim in the body**. The receiving Bot Mode agent re-interprets that `@mention` as a *bot-to-bot handoff instruction* and tries to route the message again — instead of answering the user. This is inconsistent with the **local** bot-to-bot path, where the middleware explicitly instructs the sending agent to *compose a new message* and never forward the user's text verbatim. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Desktop connected to a remote machine over SSH (Bot Mode roster shows the remote agent, e.g. `@default-homeserver`). 2. In a normal chat with the local agent, send: `@default-homeserver ping test` 3. Desktop middleware resolves the mention and delivers over Connections. The remote "Bot Chat" session receives: ``` Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): @default-homeserver ping test ``` 4. Observe the remote agent's behavior. ### Expected Behavior The mention is **routing metadata**, consumed by the sender's middleware. Once resolved, it should not reach the recipient as live syntax. The recipient should see: ``` Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): ping test ``` …and answer it as a user-origin, pre-routed message. ### Actual Behavior The remote agent treated the embedded `@default-homeserver` in the delivered body as a **handoff request aimed at itself**: 1. Composed a follow-up and ran `hermes -p default-homeserver chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q --query-file /tmp/dm_win_ping.txt` (a recursive self-delivery attempt), 2. When that failed (the profile had just been deleted), spent its turn investigating "the recipient bot no longer exists — delivery failed", 3. Never answered the actual user question ("ping test"). Verified via the remote `state.db` — full landing record: ``` 16:43:58 | user | Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): @default-homeserver ping test 16:44:29 | tool | {"output": "Background process started", "session_id": "proc_…", …} 16:44:33 | user | [IMPORTANT: Background process proc_… exited (exit code 1). Command: hermes -p default-homeserver chat …] 16:44:47 | assistant | "@default-homeserver does not exist anymore (deleted) … delivery to the destination bot failed" ``` Impact: - Wasted turns / wrong answers on every remote mention whose body echoes the handle. - **Recursion risk**: if the mentioned handle exists on the recipient, it will happily re-dispatch, potentially chaining across machines (A → B → C) with no dedup or loop guard. - Confusing UX: user gets "delivery failed" reports about a bot they successfully reached. ### Affected Component Other — Desktop app (Bot Mode mention middleware, remote delivery over Connections) ### Messaging Platform N/A (CLI only) — this is the desktop Connections channel, not a gateway platform. ### Debug Report Not attached. `hermes debug share` was run during triage, but the uploaded bundle contains tailnet IP addresses and verbatim personal chat messages, so the links were deliberately withheld from this public report. The decisive evidence for this bug is not in those logs anyway — it is (a) the remote machine's `state.db` landing record, quoted verbatim in *Actual Behavior* above, and (b) the renderer bundle's delivery code, quoted in *Root Cause Analysis*. Full logs (redacted or raw) available on request. ### Operating System Windows 11 (sender/desktop) · macOS (receiver, over SSH Connection) ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version v0.20.4 (2026.8.18) · upstream `8e77d031` · desktop build `524b0622` (built 2026-08-21T06:24Z) ### Root Cause Analysis Two independent design gaps combine: 1. **Sender side** — the remote delivery path submits the raw user text untouched (renderer bundle, remote mention delivery): ```js prompt.submit({ session_id, text: `Message from 🤖 ${senderName} (@${handle}): ${rawUserText}` }) ``` The routing mention stays inside `${rawUserText}`. 2. **Receiver side** — Bot Mode trains agents to parse incoming text for `@name` handoff requests. The envelope above is indistinguishable from a genuine bot-to-bot handoff (same emoji, same shape), so the recipient cannot tell "user message, already routed" from "another bot asking me to relay". Note the inconsistency with the **local** path: there the middleware injects explicit instructions — *"COMPOSE a message from you to that agent conveying what the user wants — do not forward this text verbatim"* — i.e. the local path already follows exactly the principle this report asks for. Only the remote path leaks the routing token. Related (all reviewed before filing; none cover the verbatim-forwarding gap): - #91339 / #91304 — handoff quoting safety (`--query-file`); different problem (shell parsing), same subsystem. - #91359 — group @mention rendering; visual layer only. - #89710 / #91340 / #91247 / #91081 — mention resolution / roster-cache fixes, all merged before this report. ### Proposed Fix Either side suffices; both is safest: - **Sender**: strip the resolved mention token(s) from the delivered text before wrapping in the envelope. For multi-mention texts (`@a tell @b …`), keep co-mentioned targets as structured metadata rather than bare tokens. - **Receiver**: define the envelope as a distinct, recognizable format (or add an explicit marker field) and instruct Bot Mode agents that anything arriving inside a Connections envelope is **user-origin and pre-routed** — never act on `@` tokens inside the quoted body. Happy to provide additional logs or test against newer builds.
signals.author: YusukeOshima-5564

signals.title: [BUG] proactive_prune_rearm_tokens invalidates prompt-cache prefix for sessions >10M tokens
signals.text: ## Summary Sessions with >10M input tokens lose 100% of prompt-cache reads under every provider path (gateway, custom:gateway, null) while small sessions cache fine at 72-93%. ## Root Cause The `_proactive_prune_rearm_tokens` mechanism in `context_compressor.py` rewrites message bodies that the provider has already seen and cached. This invalidates the cached prefix from the earliest rewritten message forward, breaking prompt-cache affinity for the entire session. ## How it happens 1. `proactive_prune_tokens=48000` (config) triggers the prune when session tokens exceed this threshold. 2. `_prune_old_tool_results()` replaces old tool output with summary strings -- **rewriting message bodies the provider has already cached**. 3. Each committed prune updates `_proactive_prune_rearm_tokens` to `after + max(reclaimed, proactive_prune_tokens, proactive_prune_min_reclaim_tokens)`. 4. For sessions >10M tokens, the prune fires repeatedly as the session grows, repeatedly rewriting the cache prefix and invalidating it each time. 5. The `proactive_prune_min_reclaim_tokens=4096` gate keeps pruning episodic but does NOT prevent cache breaks -- it only controls frequency, not the prefix-invalidation side effect. ## Reproduction 1. Configure a Hermes session with `proactive_prune_tokens: 48000` (the default). 2. Run a session that accumulates >10M input tokens (e.g., a long coding session with many tool calls returning large outputs). 3. Observe prompt-cache read tokens drop to 0% for all provider paths (gateway, custom:gateway, null). 4. Observe that small sessions (<1M tokens) cache normally at 72-93%. ## Expected behavior The proactive prune should either (a) not rewrite message bodies that the provider has already cached, or (b) advance cache breakpoints after each prune so that only the pruned portion loses cache affinity rather than the entire prefix from the earliest rewritten message. ## Actual behavior The entire prefix from the earliest rewritten message forward becomes uncacheable because the provider sees a byte-different message body at that position. ## Location - `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/context_compressor.py` -- `prune_tool_results_only()` method around line 3754-3801 - `~/.hermes/config.yaml` line 102 -- `proactive_prune_tokens: 48000` ## Layer Hermes (not LiteLLM or provider). LiteLLM correctly passes through provider cache headers; the issue is that Hermes mid-session prefix rewrites make the cached prefix byte-different from what the provider has on file. ## Evidence - ZEROCACHE row in cost-integrity-digest.py shows 0 cache-read tokens for >10M token sessions across all egress paths - Small sessions maintain 72-93% cache hit rate on all paths - The frozen >=80% rule for S1 single-egress FAILED (~44%), confirming the leak is session-size dependent, not egress-route dependent

signals.title: fix(approvals): approval prompts delivered onto a disconnected client transport time out silently — no birth log, no retry, no fallback channel
signals.text: ## Bug When a dangerous-command approval prompt is raised in a desktop (tui_gateway) session, the request is emitted as an `approval.request` event over the session's websocket transport. If that socket is dead at emit time — e.g. the client disconnected moments earlier during context compression — three things go wrong at once: 1. **No birth record.** The BLOCKED outcome lands in logs ~300s later, but nothing records that a prompt was ever raised. An operator diagnosing "why did this command get blocked?" finds only the timeout. 2. **No delivery check.** `_emit_approval_request()` writes the frame to the session transport unconditionally; a write into a closed transport fails silently (or drops), and the agent thread blocks anyway. 3. **No retry, no fallback.** There is no second attempt and no alternate channel. The 300-second `approvals.timeout` window elapses with zero human contact, then the tool returns `BLOCKED: Command timed out without user response… Silence is not consent.` This converts a consent request into a silent failure. That is safety-relevant, not cosmetic: the whole point of the approval gate is that a human sees the action before it runs. A gate that can silently not-ask is weaker than its configuration promises. ## Observed: five occurrences across two days, all silent All on one Windows install, `approvals.mode: smart`, `approvals.timeout: 300`. Each produced only the BLOCKED log line after the full timeout window; none left any record that a prompt had been raised: - **2026-08-20, 00:45 and 01:07** — two terminal-command approvals timed out at ~303s each. The user never saw a prompt on either. - **2026-08-20, 17:04** — a protected-file write approval timed out at ~300s, again unseen. - **2026-08-22, 01:27 and 01:37** — two more terminal approvals (~349s / ~363s including smart-approval assessment). This time the mechanism was caught live: - the desktop client's WS to the backend dropped at T−~80s (client-side, during a long turn); no reconnect completed; - the prompt event went onto that dead transport — no inline bar rendered, no native notification fired; - the renderer separately logged `ECONNRESET` against the backend API during the wait, confirming the wire was down; - backend logs for the entire window contain no trace of either prompt. A single occurrence could be dismissed as an unlucky race. Five across two days — including two the operator never noticed happened at all until reading the BLOCKED lines later — makes the pattern clear: **prompt delivery has no failure signal**, so every delivery failure looks identical to user silence. ## Why this matters more than a nuisance The BLOCKED message correctly forbids retrying without explicit user say-so — that policy is right, because it presumes the user *saw* the prompt and chose silence. But when delivery itself failed, nobody chose anything. The consent model currently cannot distinguish "user declined or ignored" from "user never reached." Every unacknowledged failure degrades the gate toward its own failure mode, and the operator's only recovery is noticing the BLOCKED line in a log file after the fact. ## Suggested direction Any subset of, strongest first: 1. **Birth logging**: log every approval-prompt raise (session key, pattern key, surface, timestamp) at WARNING level, symmetric with the existing BLOCKED outcome. Cheap, and makes incidents diagnosable after the fact. 2. **Delivery acknowledgement**: the client already acks prompts via `approval.received`. If no ack arrives within a short window — or the transport write fails outright — don't leave the thread blocked on a ghost; fail fast with a distinct "prompt undeliverable" error so the agent can report it instead of burning the full timeout. 3. **Fallback channel**: when the originating surface can't be reached, re-route the prompt to another registered surface for the same owner (e.g. a messaging platform already configured in the gateway). The pieces exist — adapters already implement button-based `send_exec_approval`, and `/approve` resolution is session-keyed, not surface-bound. The 300s clock should stay single across surfaces. ## Environment Windows 11, desktop app (Electron) + local `hermes serve` backends, `approvals.mode: smart`, default timeout. Happy to provide further log detail if useful.

signals.title: Hands-free voice conversation doesn't release microphone after 'stop' — wake word unresponsive until app restart
signals.text: ## Bug Description After ending a hands-free voice conversation (continuous conversation) by saying "stop", the microphone capture is not released properly. The wake word becomes unresponsive afterwards — saying it does nothing until the desktop app is fully restarted. ## Environment - Hermes Agent `v0.20.5` (2026.8.22) - Windows 11, desktop app - STT: local faster-whisper (`large-v3-turbo`, lang=zh) - Wake word: sherpa, custom Chinese wake word (single user phrase), enabled - Microphone: external USB microphone (MME host API) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable wake word + hands-free voice conversation 2. Start a hands-free conversation and speak 3. Say "stop" to end the recording/conversation 4. Try the wake word again — nothing happens (no wake detection; mic appears held/not released) ## Expected Behavior After the conversation ends, the mic capture stream is released and the wake-word detector resumes listening normally. ## Actual Behavior The wake-word detector fails to resume. Log evidence: - `logs/gui.log`: `wake.resume: detector resumed=False` after the conversation ends (normally `resumed=True` in healthy operation) - `logs/errors.log`: continuous `wake word: mic delivers only silence (peak<=10 for 10s); ... from the default input device (MME)` warnings, repeating every ~10s for 10+ minutes - `logs/desktop.log`: repeated `AudioContext encountered an error from the audio device or the WebAudio renderer` Only a full app restart releases the microphone and restores wake-word detection. ## Related - #74337 fix(desktop): voice conversation can remain muted after reply playback - #84316 Desktop app: getUserMedia fails with 'Microphone already in use' on Windows 11 - #74996 fix: wake word mic-busy retry with actionable error messages - #85770 fix(wake): stop client-capture wake from arming a deaf listener
signals.author: Xiarongyang

signals.title: Spoken reply jumps back — reads old reply from several turns ago during hands-free voice conversation (after barge-in)
signals.text: ## Bug Description In hands-free voice conversation (continuous conversation), the spoken reply occasionally **jumps back and reads an old reply from several turns ago** instead of the current response. Observed 5-6 times since yesterday on the latest desktop build. The user's own observation: it tends to happen **after a barge-in / interruption** — as if the previously interrupted speech session is never fully released and resurfaces on a later turn. ## Environment - Hermes Agent `v0.20.5` (2026.8.22) - Windows 11, desktop app - STT: local faster-whisper (`large-v3-turbo`, lang=zh) - TTS: Edge (default), hands-free mode reads every reply (hardcoded in voice-conversation mode) - Wake word: sherpa, custom Chinese wake word, enabled ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start hands-free voice conversation and hold several turns 2. During one turn's spoken reply, interrupt (barge in by speaking, or press stop) 3. Continue to the next turn 4. Occasionally the next reply is spoken **from an old turn's text** (several turns back), not the current one Frequency: intermittent, ~5-6 occurrences over a day of heavy use. Only a manual interruption (speaking over it / stop) cuts the wrong playback. ## Expected Behavior Only the current reply is spoken; interrupted/old speech sessions are fully cleaned up after barge-in. ## Actual Behavior The frontend speaks stale text from an earlier response. The agent side is healthy: `agent.log` shows every `TTS audio saved ... provider: edge` generation corresponds to the current reply (timestamped files, no ordering issue) — the bug is in the desktop playback layer, not the TTS engine. ## Code Pointers (from a quick source read) - `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.ts` - `openLiveSpeech` (~L488): streaming speech session per response; guards with `responseIdRef.current !== responseId`, but a barge-in path can leave the old session/timer around (`feedSpeechSession` interval at L552, cleared only on `session.done`) - `awaitFallbackSpeech` (~L437): whole-text fallback with a 250ms poll loop; the poll is guarded by `responseIdRef` but there is no explicit cancellation on barge-in — a stale poll could later call `playSpeechText(response.text, ...)` with an old response object - `feedSpeechSession` (~L409): appends delta text via `spokenSourceLengthRef`; if an old session is still referenced in `speechSessionRef` after interruption, a new turn can feed into the stale session - `apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-playback.ts` `playSpeechText` (L438): calls `stopVoicePlayback()` first and uses a `sequence` compare (`ownSequence === sequence`) to detect staleness — but the fallback path (`playSpeechDataUrl`) and stream-resolve windows may still race. Hypothesis: after barge-in, the interrupted speech session and its feed timer are not deterministically torn down, so a subsequent turn reuses or replays stale text. ## Related - #91987 Hands-free voice conversation doesn't release microphone after 'stop' — wake word unresponsive until app restart (same voice-mode state-machine family) - #74337 fix(desktop): voice conversation can remain muted after reply playback - #80257 fix(desktop): fix a TOCTOU race in wake-word client-capture start/stop - #85770 fix(wake): stop client-capture wake from arming a deaf listener
signals.author: Xiarongyang

signals.title: [Bug] OpenViking plugin uses uid-less viking://user/<segment> URIs that upstream removed in #4196 — will 400 on next OV release
signals.text: ## Bug Description The OpenViking memory plugin still emits **uid-less `viking://user/<segment>` URIs**, a spelling that upstream OpenViking **removed in commit #4196** (`feat(uri)!: remove uid-less current-user shorthand in favor of viking://~`, merged 2026-08-21 into main). Per the upstream BREAKING CHANGE note, requests using that spelling now fail with **HTTP 400** (`NamespaceShapeError`) — the server no longer expands `viking://user/<reserved-segment>` to the current user's space. Affected hardcoded URIs in `plugins/memory/openviking/__init__.py`: - L96 `_PROFILE_URI = "viking://user/memories/profile.md"` - L97 `_PREFERENCES_URI = "viking://user/memories/preferences"` - L98 `_ENTITIES_URI = "viking://user/memories/entities"` - L4782 `_build_memory_uri()` → `viking://user/peers/{agent}/memories/{subdir}/mem_{slug}.md` - L576 tool description example string (`viking://user/memories/`) - README.md references to `viking://user/peers/...` All of these flow through the REST API (`/api/v1/content/read`, `/api/v1/content/write`). On the OpenViking server every content endpoint validates via `validate_request_viking_uri` → `resolve_request_uri` → `resolve_current_user_uri`, which **rejects** `viking://user/<segment>` when the segment is a reserved name (`memories`, `resources`, `skills`, `peers`, `privacy`, `sessions`) and differs from the caller's user_id. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run an OpenViking server built from current main (contains #4196), or wait for the next release after 0.4.16. 2. Start Hermes with the OpenViking memory provider (trusted mode, no API key; local ovcli config with `actor_peer_id: hermes`). 3. Any session start or memory write triggers the plugin's REST calls with the old URI spelling. ## Expected Behavior - Session-start profile/preferences/entities reads succeed. - `on_memory_write` mirroring writes succeed. - Works with the current OpenViking release AND future releases. ## Actual Behavior - All requests using `viking://user/memories/...` / `viking://user/peers/...` return 400 from the server → profile/preferences/entities never reach the model context, and memory mirroring silently fails. - Today it does not crash only because the locally installed server is 0.4.15 (released before #4196). PyPI 0.4.16 (2026-08-21) also predates #4196, so it still accepts the old spelling — but the next OpenViking release will break the plugin. ## Root Cause Analysis OpenViking introduced `viking://~` as the unambiguous current-user home alias in #4167 (merged 2026-08-20, included in the 0.4.16 release), then removed the ambiguous uid-less shorthand in #4196 (merged 2026-08-21, main only). Upstream migrated all first-party clients (vikingbot, langchain, openclaw, dsh, pi plugin, etc.) to `viking://~/...` in the same PR. The Hermes plugin is a third-party client that was not migrated. ## Proposed Fix Replace the uid-less spellings with the `viking://~` home alias in `plugins/memory/openviking/__init__.py` (and README): - `viking://~/memories/profile.md` - `viking://~/memories/preferences` - `viking://~/memories/entities` - `viking://~/peers/{agent}/memories/{subdir}/mem_{slug}.md` Notes: - `viking://~` requires OpenViking server >= 0.4.16 (alias landed in #4167). Older servers (0.4.15) will not understand it — but they still accept the old spelling, so the change is safe once the server is on 0.4.16+. - In trusted mode the plugin's identity is `account=default, user=default, actor_peer=hermes`, so `~` expands to `viking://user/default/...` — identical to the current on-disk layout (`viking/default/user/default/memories/profile.md`), so no data migration is needed. - The `viking://user/peers/{agent}/...` write path in `_build_memory_uri()` is affected too (peers is also a reserved segment) — this one is the most impactful because it is the memory-mirroring write path.

signals.title: [Bug]: delegation live transcripts resolve HERMES_HOME after a thread hop and can write to another profile
signals.text: ### Bug description In a multi-profile process, `delegate_task` live-transcript files can be written under a different profile from the session that initiated the delegation. Observed on Hermes Agent **v0.19.1 (v2026.7.30)**: one session running as profile `generic-core` produced delegation transcripts under both: ```text /root/.hermes/profiles/generic-core/cache/delegation/live/ /root/.hermes/profiles/thindi/cache/delegation/live/ ``` The destination varied with concurrent worker timing. The relevant code is unchanged in v0.20.5 (`v2026.8.19`) and current `main` (`b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff` as checked on 2026-08-22). ### Expected behavior Every delegation artifact created by a session should be rooted under that session's resolved profile home, regardless of thread scheduling or concurrent sessions on other profiles. ### Actual behavior `tools/delegation_live_log.py:61-65` resolves the root implicitly: ```python def live_transcript_root() -> Path: """Root directory for live transcripts (profile-safe, never ~/.hermes).""" from hermes_constants import get_hermes_dir return get_hermes_dir("cache/delegation", "delegation_cache") / "live" ``` `get_hermes_dir()` therefore uses ambient `get_hermes_home()` state. If the call runs after a raw `threading.Thread` boundary, the originating `_HERMES_HOME_OVERRIDE` value is absent because `ContextVar` values do not automatically propagate to new threads. Resolution falls through to process-wide `HERMES_HOME` or the default home. In a multi-profile WebUI process, process-wide `HERMES_HOME` is also unsuitable as a session identity because concurrent workers temporarily change it for different profiles. ### Deterministic reproduction This reproduces without a model call and writes only under a temporary directory: ```python import os import tempfile import threading from pathlib import Path from hermes_constants import ( reset_hermes_home_override, set_hermes_home_override, ) from tools.delegation_live_log import create_live_transcripts with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td: td = Path(td) process_home = td / "process-default-thindi" session_home = td / "session-generic-core" process_home.mkdir() session_home.mkdir() old = os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME") os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(process_home) token = set_hermes_home_override(session_home) out = {} try: def worker(): _id, _writers, paths = create_live_transcripts( [{"goal": "profile path repro"}] ) out["path"] = paths[0] thread = threading.Thread(target=worker) thread.start() thread.join() finally: reset_hermes_home_override(token) if old is None: os.environ.pop("HERMES_HOME", None) else: os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = old actual = Path(out["path"]) expected_root = session_home / "cache/delegation/live" wrong_root = process_home / "cache/delegation/live" print("actual_path=", actual) print("expected_under_session=", actual.is_relative_to(expected_root)) print("actual_under_process_default=", actual.is_relative_to(wrong_root)) ``` Observed output on v0.19.1: ```text actual_path= /tmp/.../process-default-thindi/cache/delegation/live/deleg_.../task-0.log expected_under_session= False actual_under_process_default= True ``` A minimal `ContextVar` control also confirms the boundary behavior: ```text plain threading.Thread: process/default value copy_context().run(thread target): session/profile value ``` ### Root cause `hermes_constants.py` defines `_HERMES_HOME_OVERRIDE` as a `ContextVar` and `get_hermes_home()` correctly consults it first. The missing invariant is that profile identity is not explicitly carried across every concurrency boundary before profile-scoped paths are resolved. `get_hermes_dir()` already documents the intended contract: ```text home: Optional explicit Hermes home. Profile-aware callers that manage more than one home in the same process use this instead of temporarily mutating the process or context-local HERMES_HOME. ``` However, `delegation_live_log.live_transcript_root()` does not pass `home=`. The delegation fan-out itself uses `contextvars.copy_context()` for its child executor tasks, but that is too late to repair a profile context already lost when the parent agent turn entered through an earlier raw thread boundary. It also does not make process-global `os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]` safe for concurrent profiles. ### Suggested fix Prefer explicit profile-home threading for profile-scoped delegation artifacts: 1. Resolve the delegation home from stable parent-owned state at `delegate_task` entry. On current Hermes, the parent's profile-specific `SessionDB.db_path.parent` is one available source; an explicit `profile_home` field on the agent would be cleaner. 2. Add a `home: Path | None` parameter to `live_transcript_root()` / `create_live_transcripts()`. 3. Call: ```python get_hermes_dir( "cache/delegation", "delegation_cache", home=resolved_profile_home, ) ``` 4. Add a regression test that creates a session-home override, crosses a raw thread boundary with a different process `HERMES_HOME`, and asserts every transcript/manifest path stays under the session home. Capturing `contextvars.copy_context()` at every raw thread spawn is useful defense in depth, especially in WebUI/desktop entry points, but explicit `home=` is the stronger storage-boundary fix because it does not depend on ambient context surviving future executor/thread refactors. ### Impact - Cross-profile leakage of operational transcripts, goals, tool arguments/results, and metadata. - Missing live logs in the initiating profile and misleading paths returned to the parent. - Non-deterministic behavior under concurrent profile activity. - Profile deletion/retention can affect artifacts owned by another profile. The transcript redactor reduces credential exposure, but writing a profile's operational data into another profile remains an isolation violation. ### Related upstream work - #18594 — broader wrong-profile fallback class. - #88715 — canonical profile identity must survive async/thread boundaries. - #77015 — live-transcript path visibility for Docker/remote backends; different root cause. - #81267 / merged PR #86668 — v0.19.1 delegated children borrowed the parent's `SessionDB`; fixed after v0.19.1 with child-owned connections at the parent's `db_path`. - #91610 / PR #91631 — newer shared launch-`SessionDB` ownership variant causing `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'execute'`; separate from this live-log path defect. ### Environment - Hermes Agent: v0.19.1 (`v2026.7.30`) - Install method: git / Hermes WebUI combined runtime - OS: Linux - Python: 3.12.13 - Multi-profile process: `generic-core` and `thindi` 🤖 This was written by an AI coding agent
