signals.title: fix(tui): print the auto-compaction lifecycle into the transcript
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? The compaction lifecycle reaches the TUI under **three** different `kind` values, from three different producers, all meaning the same thing to the user: *part of your conversation was rewritten.* | `kind` | when | producer | |---|---|---| | `compressing` | manual `/compress` progress | `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` | | `compacting` | auto-compaction started | `tui_gateway/server.py::_status_update` re-tags the generic `lifecycle` status that carries `COMPACTION_STATUS_MARKER` | | `compacted` | auto-compaction finished | `agent/conversation_compression.py::_emit_compaction_done` | The transcript branch in `createGatewayEventHandler` matched exactly one of them: ```ts if (p.kind === 'compressing') { sys(p.text) return } ``` So the compaction the user **did not ask for**, the one that most needs explaining because the transcript appears to reset itself mid-turn, left no durable record. It set the status bar and pushed a per-turn activity entry, and then `restoreStatusAfter(4000)` wiped the status four seconds later. Scroll up afterwards and there is nothing to say why the history changed. Manual `/compress`, the case the user already knows about, was the only one that left a line. The desktop client already handles all three kinds (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts:1417-1420`, with tests in `compaction-event.test.tsx`), so this is the TUI catching up to a contract the other client already honors. **On the "aborted compaction" half of the issue.** I did not fix that here, and I want to be precise about why rather than quietly narrowing scope. An aborted compaction is not silent: `conversation_compression.py` calls `agent._emit_warning("⚠ Compression aborted: ...")`, which reaches `status_callback("warn", ...)` and does land in the status bar and the activity strip. What it does not get is a transcript line, for the same reason as the other two. But `warn` is a **generic** kind carrying every warning the agent emits, so widening the match to `warn` would print every unrelated warning into the transcript, and giving the abort its own kind means changing the Python emitter for a value that the desktop app, the chat gateways and the gateway noise filter all consume. That is a cross-surface design call and it is yours to make. Happy to do it in a follow-up once you pick the shape. ## Related Issue Refs #88102 (deliberately a **subset**: this fixes the kind mismatch, not the aborted-compaction half, so the issue should stay open). Reported by @mayqhw. Note that the reporter opened #88098 for this and **closed it themselves one minute later** ("the fix is a stopgap; the proper solution needs upstream design"), so this PR does not duplicate live work. I have deliberately kept the change to the kind mismatch and left the richer "structured compaction progress event" idea from the issue to a maintainer. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `ui-tui/src/app/createGatewayEventHandler.ts` — new module constant `COMPACTION_TRANSCRIPT_KINDS` (`compacted`, `compacting`, `compressing`) with a comment naming each producer, so the next person adding a kind sees the whole family in one place instead of rediscovering the re-tag in `server.py`. The membership test drives `sys(p.text)`. - `ui-tui/src/__tests__/createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts` — 3 tests, added beside the existing `compressing` one. **The two new kinds keep the status-bar and activity handling they have today.** This only *adds* the transcript line; `compressing` keeps its exact early return. Routing the new kinds through that early return instead would have been tidier code, but it drops their activity entry and pins `✓ Context compaction complete` in the status bar until the next status arrives, since the `compressing` path never calls `restoreStatusAfter`. Two of the new tests assert the activity entry precisely so that regression cannot be introduced later as a cleanup. No Python is touched, and no other event kind changes behavior. ## How to Test ``` cd ui-tui npm run build:ink npx vitest run src/__tests__/createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts ``` 104 passed (101 before this PR). Mutation check, one rule at a time, to show each test is tied to its rule: | Mutation | Result | |---|---| | Narrow the set back to `['compressing']` | **2 failed**, 102 passed (both new positive tests) | | Match any non-empty kind (`if (Boolean(p.kind))`) | **1 failed**, 103 passed (the new negative test) | | Route the new kinds through the `compressing` early return | **2 failed**, 102 passed (both activity assertions) | Also clean: - `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — exit 0 - `eslint` on both files — exit 0 - `prettier --check` on both files — clean Full `ui-tui` suite: 1645 passed, 10 failed, 5 skipped. **All 10 failures are pre-existing and unrelated** (`editor.test.ts` resolves `nano`/`vi` off `$PATH`, `terminalSetup`/`terminalParity` assert POSIX config dirs). I verified this by stashing only my two files and re-running those three files on a pristine tree: the same 10 fail identically. They are Windows-environment failures, not regressions. Manual check of the real path, for anyone reproducing: the auto-compaction line the TUI now keeps is `🗜️ Compacting context — summarizing earlier conversation so I can continue...` followed by `✓ Context compaction complete — continuing turn...`, matching `COMPACTION_STATUS` / `COMPACTION_DONE_STATUS`. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — checked the issue timeline, open and merged PR search, and every open PR with `compaction` in its title for overlap with `ui-tui/src/app/`; none touch this file - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — N/A, no Python is touched; the JS equivalents are in *How to Test* - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — the new constant documents all three producers and why the family exists - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A. Worth noting that `compression.progress_notices` gates routine compression notices for *chat platforms* in `gateway/run.py`; it does not gate `tui_gateway`'s `status.update` stream, so this change adds no new config surface and prints only statuses the gateway already sends. - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure string matching on an event field, no platform-dependent behavior - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs Before, on `main`, an auto-compaction leaves the transcript with nothing between the two turns it split: ``` status.update { kind: 'compacting', text: '🗜️ Compacting context — ...' } -> status bar only, gone after 4s status.update { kind: 'compacted', text: '✓ Context compaction complete...' } -> status bar only, gone after 4s ``` After, both land via `sys()` alongside the manual `/compress` line that already worked, and the status bar and activity strip behave exactly as before.

signals.title: feat: unify agent isolation (--ignore-rules / --safe-mode) across TUI, messaging gateway, and API server
signals.text: ## Problem `--ignore-rules` / `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES` and `--safe-mode` / `HERMES_SAFE_MODE` are honored by CLI chat and `-z` oneshot sessions, but not consistently by the other agent session entry points. On current `main`: - TUI session agents read only `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES`; `HERMES_SAFE_MODE` is ignored for the skip flags, and TUI background turns do not inherit the parent session's isolation. - The messaging gateway only supports an opt-in per-platform `gateway.platforms.<platform>.skip_context_files` config; both env vars are ignored on foreground turns and background tasks. - The API server constructs `AIAgent` without either skip flag and never reads the env vars. - CLI background tasks and ACP (Agent Client Protocol) sessions construct `AIAgent` without the skip flags. ## Root cause Isolation intent is resolved per entry point instead of once. `--ignore-rules` and `--safe-mode` are normalized to `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES` / `HERMES_SAFE_MODE` at CLI startup, but the other agent construction sites never resolve them, so `AIAgent` receives default `False` skip flags and injects rules/memory even when isolation was requested. ## Scope Included: - `agent/isolation.py`: one private resolver, precedence = explicit flag > env (`HERMES_IGNORE_RULES`, `HERMES_SAFE_MODE`; safe mode implies ignore-rules) > default `False`; returns `(skip_context_files, skip_memory)`. - TUI session agent construction (`tui_gateway/server.py`, `_make_agent`) and TUI background/preview turns (`_background_agent_kwargs`). - Messaging gateway foreground turns and background tasks (`gateway/run.py`), including the agent cache signature so a cached `AIAgent` is never reused across an isolation change. - API server agent construction (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`). - CLI background tasks (`hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`). - ACP session agents (`acp_adapter/session.py`). - Docs and per-entry behavior tests. Not included (follow-ups): `-z` oneshot / Termux wiring (tracked in #72075, kept independent; can be refactored onto the shared resolver after it merges); cron / batch / curator / delegate worker policies (deliberate internal contracts); new `config.yaml` keys (public config surface, only if maintainers want it). ## Design One resolver as the single source of truth. For the gateway, isolation composes with the existing per-platform latency opt-out: `skip_context_files = isolation OR platform config`, `skip_memory = isolation`. Default behavior is unchanged everywhere. ## Coverage matrix | Entry | Before | After | Test | |---|---|---|---| | CLI chat | env honored | unchanged | existing | | CLI oneshot / Termux | #72075 | unchanged (merged separately) | #72075 | | CLI background task | neither | both | resolver contract + review | | TUI session | `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES` only | both env vars | `test_make_agent_forwards_isolation_env` | | TUI background turn | no inheritance | inherits parent session | `test_background_agent_kwargs_inherits_isolation` | | Messaging gateway foreground | per-platform config only | config OR isolation; cache signature includes both skip flags | `test_skip_context_files_change_different_signature`, `test_skip_memory_change_different_signature`, `test_resolve_gateway_isolation_skip_flags` | | Messaging gateway background task | neither | both | `test_resolve_gateway_isolation_skip_flags` | | API server | neither | both | `test_create_agent_honors_isolation_env` | | ACP session | neither | both | `test_make_agent_forwards_isolation_env`, `test_make_agent_defaults_isolation_off` | ## Compatibility - Default behavior: unchanged (resolver returns `False` when no flag/env is set). - Existing config: the gateway per-platform `skip_context_files` key keeps working and composes with isolation. - Public API: no public interface or config format changes. - Session cache: `skip_memory` now participates in the gateway agent cache signature, so an isolation toggle rebuilds the agent instead of silently reusing a stale one. ## Related / competing work - Scope proposal: #88214 - Canonical oneshot issues (open): #26633, #72064 - Oneshot fix kept independent: #72075 - Earlier partial oneshot fixes (open, not updated): #26771, #59402 - #29930: earlier partial gateway-only fix for `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES` (stale base, not updated since 2026-07). This PR covers that gateway path plus safe mode, background tasks, cache invalidation, TUI, CLI background, API server, and ACP via the shared resolver. ## Validation | Command | Result | |---|---| | `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_isolation.py tests/gateway/test_isolation_skip_flags.py tests/gateway/test_agent_cache.py tests/acp/test_session.py` | passed | | `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` | 573+ passed | | `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_api_server.py` | passed | | `ruff check` on changed files | passed | | `git diff --check` | clean |

signals.title: fix(security): memory prefetch quarantine/finalization — rebuild required
signals.text: ## Current source of truth — draft / do not merge Live head: `578697343ede8691200aad8ef9ae79b466d942e4`. The submitted branch is no longer the historical three-file quarantine repair candidate. GitHub currently reports **965 commits / 1,384 changed files** against `main`; the head is topology-polluted and cannot serve as a reviewable security object. This PR has therefore been returned to **draft** rather than leaving a superficially mergeable but non-authoritative object exposed for landing. The previously documented head `a8279f3d083145dfa77a3eeb2ad7e50e10bd658b` and its local patch receipts are historical only. ## Required security contract A correct replacement still has to prove all of the following: - once an external provider misses `external_prefetch_timeout`, quarantine that provider for the lifetime of the owning `MemoryManager` instance; - late completion retires the detached worker handle but never restores trust or reopens the provider; - all later sensitive fanout paths fail closed, including synchronous and queued prefetch, sync, tool calls, turn/session/compression hooks, write mirroring, delegation, and re-initialization; - work queued before timeout re-checks quarantine at execution time; - shutdown remains permitted for cleanup/cancellation hooks; and - a finalization fence prevents a concurrent turn from starting a fresh external call between worker completion and timeout-owner quarantine. The already-dispatched provider call still cannot be revoked by Python; this remains exposure-limiting quarantine, not a claim of full cancellation. ## Historical reviewed artifact The prior independently reviewed local repair was recorded as: - `pr88796-current-head-security-ci-fix.patch`; - target `a8279f3d083145dfa77a3eeb2ad7e50e10bd658b`; - SHA-256 `0018a5a972f19b4f8e20a8ed5760d2c9403614bcd97efd52f0da61955a5f00e7`; - three files, 268 insertions / 53 deletions; - 16 focused MemoryManager/async-sync tests; - 500 repeated quarantine-lifecycle iterations; - 100 queued-before-quarantine race iterations; - compile / diff checks clean. Restack onto exact current `main` as a small reviewable object; do not retain the 1,384-file branch topology. 3. Remove unrelated branch churn. 4. signals.title: fix(desktop): prevent remote config overwrite & preserve basic auth credentials (#88913)
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #88913 where Hermes Desktop, when connected to an authenticated remote backend, autosaved a stale local/default config snapshot over the remote server's `config.yaml` upon browsing or saving Settings. ### Root Cause 1. **Stale Cache Lock-In**: React Query cached the local config record under `['hermes-config-record']`. On gateway connection swap, components like `ConfigSettings` mounted with the stale local config before background refetch finished, setting `configSeeded.current = true` and ignoring subsequent remote fetches. 2. **Full Snapshot Clobbering**: Desktop sent a full `HermesConfigRecord` snapshot in `PUT /api/config`. The server's `_deep_merge` overwrote remote `config.yaml` fields with Desktop's un-edited local defaults. 3. **Basic Auth Erasure**: Generic serialization sent empty strings `""` for `dashboard.basic_auth`, erasing basic auth credentials on the remote backend. ### Fix - **Revision / ETag Tracking**: `GET /api/config` attaches a 16-character SHA-256 `_revision` token. `PUT /api/config` checks `expected_revision` and returns **HTTP 409 Conflict** on stale writes. - **Security Boundary Shield**: Added `_protect_sensitive_config_fields` in `web_server.py` to prevent empty string overwrites of `dashboard.basic_auth` credentials. - **Desktop Cache Purging**: Added `resetHermesConfigCache()` called during `wipeSessionListsForGatewaySwitch()` to clear query caches on connection re-home. - **Re-seeding**: Draft re-synchronizes when a fresh remote `_revision` lands if `saveVersion === 0`. ### Verification & Stress Benchmarks - **Unit Tests**: Added `test_remote_config_protection.py` (4 passed). - **Web Server Suite**: 159 tests passed. - **Stress Load Benchmark**: `test_config_endpoint_stress.py` demonstrated **140.8 req/sec** read throughput (69.17 ms avg latency) and 100% CAS safety (20 atomic writes, 80 revision conflict 409 rejections, 0 errors). Closes #88913 ## Infographic :

signals.title: fix(copilot): preserve signed thinking across tool results
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? It preserves Claude signed-thinking blocks when the Anthropic Messages adapter is pointed at GitHub Copilot's `/v1/messages` relay. The adapter currently treats every non-Anthropic host except Nous Portal as signature-blind and strips all thinking blocks. Copilot implements Claude's signed-thinking contract end to end: a response can contain `thinking + signature + tool_use`, and the next request must replay that assistant block unchanged together with the tool result. Stripping the block loses reasoning continuity and violates the endpoint's replay contract. This change classifies Copilot hosts with hostname-safe matching and lets the latest assistant turn follow the native signed-thinking replay path. Generic third-party proxies keep the existing stripping behavior. ## Related Issue Related to #57625. That PR enables the default catalog route to `/v1/messages`; this PR fixes the adapter-level replay behavior required once that route is used. signals.title: feat(memory): add rationale-attached provenance tail convention to MEMORY_GUIDANCE
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds a compact provenance-tail convention to `MEMORY_GUIDANCE` so durable memory entries carry a `[why: ...]` tail naming the concrete failure or observation they prevent, with enforcements against vacuous rationales and a mention of the `apply_batch` operations escape hatch for the "add at capacity" workflow. This is Phase 1 of issue #86022 — the prompt-layer change that attaches rationale at write time. It does not add a new schema, file layout, or tool. Phase 2 (curator premise-evaluation) is out of scope for this PR. ## Related Issue Fixes #86022 ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests - [ ] ♻️ Refactor - [ ] 🎯 New skill ## Changes Made - **`agent/prompt_builder.py`** — extends `MEMORY_GUIDANCE`: - Replaces the "write declarative facts" paragraph with a provenance-tail convention: every durable entry carries a short `[why: ...]` tail naming the concrete failure/observation it prevents, plus the date when known - Adds concrete ALLOW examples (resolver.py + RuntimeError) and a REJECT list for vacuous tails (`[why: useful]`, `[why: best practice]`, `[why: see above]`, `[why: to be safe]`) — rationales without a concrete failure are rejected at write time, not written - Adds a short "where the date comes from" section: dated events get YYYY-MM-DD; undated stable facts omit the date rather than invent one; never backfill an unanchorable date - Notes the tail's purpose: provenance signal for later deletion decisions (issue #86022 Phase 2), NOT a changelog entry for rollback (issue #81015) - Notes the tail lives in the existing §-delimited ledger format — no schema change, no front matter, no new file layout - Mentions the `apply_batch` operations escape hatch as the recommended tool when memory is full and a new rationale-attached entry needs to be added (free space + add in one call, final-budget-checked; references #79414 for docs on the escape hatch) ## How to Test 1. Install the change into a Hermes home: `cp agent/prompt_builder.py ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py` (or use the shared clone as the HERMES_HOME source). 2. Open a session with the modified `MEMORY_GUIDANCE` active. 3. Add a durable memory entry. Confirm the entry's text includes a `[why: ...]` tail that names a concrete failure or observation, not a vacuous tag like `[why: useful]`. 4. Attempt to add an entry with a vacuous tail (e.g. `[why: useful]`). The guidance should steer the agent to reject and reword rather than commit a decorative rationale. (This is guidance-level enforcement, not a tool hard gate — the model is instructed to reject before committing.) 5. Confirm existing entries without tails are not altered — the guidance applies to new writes, not retroactive edits. 6. Confirm the char budget behavior is unchanged: `apply_batch` is mentioned for the "add at capacity" workflow but the budget enforcement in `memory_tool.py` is unmodified. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] Read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] Commit message follows [Conventional Commits] (`feat(memory): add rationale-attached provenance tail convention to MEMORY_GUIDANCE`) - [x] Searched for existing PRs — none addressing this prompt-layer change (issues #86022, #81015, #79414 exist but no PR yet) - [x] PR contains only changes related to this feature (one file, `MEMORY_GUIDANCE` only) - [x] Run `pytest tests/ -q` — memory/tool/prompt_builder slices all pass (41 passed in `test_memory_tool.py`, all green in `test_prompt_builder.py`; one pre-existing failure in `test_hindsight_provider.py` is unrelated — reproduces on `main` without this change; it's a mock fixture issue in a Hindsight prefetch/retain async ordering test) - [ ] Tests for the change — N/A for this PR: this is a prompt-guidance change, not a code behavior change. The guidance is exercised implicitly by any session that writes memory. A future PR could add a smoke test that checks `MEMORY_GUIDANCE` contains the `[why: ...]` tail convention. ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [ ] Updated relevant docs — N/A. The `MEMORY.md` user-guide doc already describes the §-delimited ledger format; no doc change is required for this guidance-only PR. - [ ] Updated `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no config keys changed) - [ ] Updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` — N/A (no architecture/workflow change) - [x] Considered cross-platform impact — N/A (plaintext guidance, platform-independent) - [ ] Updated tool descriptions/schemas — N/A (no tool behavior changed; `apply_batch` is mentioned in guidance but its schema/handler are unmodified) ## Notes for Reviewers - This is Phase 1 of #86022 only. Phase 2 (curator using the `[why:]` tail for premise-evaluation and deletion-surface decisions) is out of scope. - The tail convention intentionally lives in the existing §-delimited ledger format. No front matter, no schema, no new file layout — the cheapest phase of the proposal and the only one in scope for this PR. - The REJECT list for vacuous tails is the load-bearing detail: without it, the guidance risks injecting decorative `[why: useful]` entries that increase char consumption per entry with zero deletion signal. The guidance enforces concrete failures/observations or no write. - `apply_batch` (the batch "operations" escape hatch) is mentioned because that's the existing tool for the "free space + add new entry at capacity" workflow — the issue description does not mention it and #79414 is a doc gap about the escape hatch. - Evidence framing: arXiv:2608.11095 is cited in the issue as adjacent motivation for the shared root cause (no rationale → deletion feels unsafe). The paper measured repo instruction-file accretion (CLAUDE.md-style, commit-time), not Hermes' per-session char-budget ledger. Hermes' actual failure mode is truncation-by-crisis + stale entries kept unsafely because deletion feels unverifiable. This PR does not re-litigate that in the guidance text (the guidance is operational, not evidentiary), but the framing is stated here for reviewer context. - **Known seam issue:** the background-review writer currently writes only to built-in MEMORY.md and ignores the configured Hindsight provider (issues #56464 and #59244). This PR is scoped to the built-in layer as #86022's Phase 1 does. The provider-side question — whether ledger `[why:]` tails should also reach Hindsight, or whether the two layers should remain separate for different consumers — is acknowledged here as a known seam issue, not resolved by this PR. The provider-side alignment is a separate decision for a later pass (or for #56464's resolution to change what the writer targets).

signals.title: fix(desktop): preserve authoritative connectionId, fail-closed legacy fallbacks — #90048
signals.text: ## Summary Make #90198 the single current-main integration owner for Desktop connection identity. This composes both required halves of the repair: - #90913's explicit-qualification rule: once a descriptor contains a `connectionId` property, only an exact ID in the current registry is accepted; blank, null, undefined, non-string, unknown, and retired values fail closed without endpoint fallback. - #90198's full-envelope compatibility rule: only genuinely unqualified legacy descriptors may be matched, using the shared URL/Cloud or SSH identity envelope, with zero or multiple matches unresolved. Closes #90048. ## Root cause and production evidence #89719 established registry-scoped routing, but the compatibility bridge could still weaken identity after dialing and reconstruct it from mutable transport-shaped metadata. There are two boundaries: 1. A registry-qualified descriptor must retain an exact, current connection ID. Invalid explicit qualification must never become permission to infer another source. 2. A genuinely unqualified legacy descriptor must never acquire identity through first-match URL or `user@host` selection. @AndreasG78's [production macOS + remote-primary reproduction](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/90048#issuecomment-5375227679) adds evidence for an earlier shipped-release boundary: in the v0.20.5 bundle they inspected, Bot wake entered legacy `hermes:connection`, attempted a local `ensureBackend()`, and failed before `resolvedConnectionId()` could run. Their narrow stopgap eliminated 177 observed local-profile failures in that topology. That result corroborates caller misqualification; it does not make `missing local directory + registry primary` canonical ownership proof. That inference is unsafe with multiple remotes, a non-primary owner, a changed primary, or a retired registration. The stopgap is credited but not included here; it may be considered separately as a maintenance backport. ## Contract - Presence of a `connectionId` property means the descriptor claims registry qualification. - A nonblank string is accepted only when it exactly names a current registry entry. - Blank, null, undefined, non-string, unknown, and retired explicit IDs return `null`. - Explicit-ID rejection never falls through to endpoint inference. - Only descriptors with no `connectionId` property enter legacy compatibility. - URL/Cloud identity includes kind, normalized URL, auth mode, token envelope, canonical headers, and Cloud organization. - SSH identity includes normalized host/user, defaulted port, key path, remote Hermes path, and remote profile. - Zero or multiple coarse candidates and zero or multiple full-envelope matches fail closed. - Registry order never changes a verdict. - Registry-primary restoration passes the exact `(connectionId, profile)` tuple into the gateway path. ## Acceptance matrix | Input | Required result | |---|---| | Current exact ID with contradictory URL or SSH metadata | Return that exact ID | | Explicit blank/null/undefined/non-string/unknown/retired ID with otherwise inferable metadata | `null`; no fallback | | No ID property; one complete legacy URL/Cloud/SSH match | Return the unique ID | | No ID property; zero, weakly ambiguous, or exact-twin matches | `null` | | Registry reordered | Same verdict | | Remote registry primary restored while the active descriptor is local | Activate the remote primary by exact ID | | Packaged remote-primary setup with no local profile directory | Use the qualified route; do not infer ownership from primary selection | ## Implementation - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-route-identity.ts` owns the shared full-envelope matcher derived from #88922. - `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-remote-route.ts` consumes that matcher for pre-dial route selection. - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-registry.ts` implements property-presence/current-registry authority and ambiguity-safe legacy inference. - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-registry.test.ts` covers explicit-ID validity, local cardinality, URL/Cloud/SSH collisions, mixed-case SSH normalization, and order invariance. - `apps/desktop/src/store/connections.test.ts` proves remote-primary restoration calls `ensureGatewayAgent(primaryId, "default")` and records that exact ID. No `main.ts` or `profile-delete-routing.ts` primary-selection heuristic is added. ## Verification Exact head: `9773a3dd37530024df2d915d2e1e2339ecc6153d` Exact base: `2ea5287da0ed3556110e5e5c88210b41db19ec6d` Passed locally after the final rebase: - focused Electron: 2 files, 78/78 tests; - adjacent UI caller/lifecycle: 4 files, 35/35 tests; - `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`; - `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`; - targeted ESLint; - `git diff --check`; - contributor-attribution audit; - Windows-footgun scan. Broader sweep receipts: - Electron: 111 files passed, 1 skipped; 1576/1580 tests passed, 3 skipped. One unrelated `remote-lifecycle.test.ts` test cannot run because this sandbox's own `ps -p $$` fails with `fatal library error, lookup self`; the file is unchanged from `main`. - UI: 563/565 files passed; 5379/5382 tests passed. The remaining model-menu timeouts/assertion and one cross-test timer error are outside the changed paths; the affected Skills test passed 11/11 when rerun serially. Hosted exact-head acceptance: - [CI](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32533462264): success; - [Docker](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32533461798): success; - [Nix](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32533461760): success. ## Topology and provenance - Prior work by @teknium1 in #89719 supplied the registry-scoped routing foundation. - Prior work by @teknium1 in #88922 supplied the canonical full-envelope matcher. - Prior work by @andrexibiza in #90913 supplied the property-presence/current-registry fail-closed invariant and focused witnesses. - Prior evidence by @AndreasG78 in the [exact #90048 comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/90048#issuecomment-5375227679) supplied the independent production reproduction and tested stopgap. - #90198 is the surviving integration surface. - #90913 was closed unmerged as superseded after this exact head passed CI, Docker, and Nix. - @saralilyb's #90006 and #90924 should consume/rebase on this identity owner rather than add another resolver. - @bblicke1's #89769 overlaps registry files but owns disjoint roster semantics; whichever lands later should rebase.

signals.title: fix(agent): detect tool-call argument and result jitter
signals.text: ## Summary Follow-up to #90338 and the scoped request in #85323. The merged `observe_identical_call()` guard catches exact repeats, but explicit no-progress representations could still mint a fresh observation: 1. A declarative `todo` call can jitter `merge: true` / `false` while re-asserting the same ordered task state. 2. `read_file` and `skill_view` can replace a full result with an explicit unchanged envelope (`status: "unchanged"`, `dedup: true`, `content_returned: false`). The envelope hashes differently even though it certifies that the underlying result did not change. This change: - gives the observational stall guard a narrowly normalized signature for `todo`, ignoring only `merge`; - keeps todo item order significant because it defines priority; - carries the consecutive streak through a validated unchanged/dedup envelope, scoped to the tools that actually emit that contract (`read_file`, `skill_view`); - anchors the streak on its original result hash, so a loop alternating full payload ↔ dedup stub still reaches the threshold while a genuinely changed result resets it; - resets normally for lookalike payloads missing the full dedup contract; - leaves all other tools, failure/no-progress signatures, and poller exemptions unchanged. ## Test plan - [x] Canonical runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/agent/test_stall_guards.py tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py tests/tools/test_skill_view_dedup.py` — 43 passed, 0 failed - [x] `ruff check agent/tool_guardrails.py tests/agent/test_stall_guards.py` - [x] Mutation check: removing todo signature normalization fails the todo jitter regression - [x] Mutation check: removing explicit unchanged-result handling fails the result-jitter regression - [x] Independent adversarial review of the state machine; findings (full↔stub alternation reset, unscoped envelope contract) fixed in `8d74772` with regression tests - [x] Broader file-tool suite attempted: 84 passed, 2 skipped, 2 unrelated macOS `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp` mock-path failures - [x] Remote branch head verified after push Closes the additive arg/result-jitter gap identified in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/85323#issuecomment-5350440406

signals.title: fix(cli): label standalone dashboard holders correctly in the venv message
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? When `hermes update` refuses the dependency step because something else runs from the install's venv, the holder list mislabeled a standalone `hermes dashboard` process as **"Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app)"** (#90778). `serve` and `dashboard` shared one classification branch, but they are different things: `hermes serve` is the headless backend the Electron app spawns (closing the desktop app clears it), while `hermes dashboard` is the standalone browser UI on port 9119 that a user starts themselves — only the first is "the desktop app". The advice therefore pointed at a program that may not even be running while the actual holder kept the venv locked, and the remedy line never mentioned `hermes dashboard --stop`, the only thing that clears this holder. This PR splits the branch: `serve` keeps the desktop-backend hint, `dashboard` gets a standalone label naming `hermes dashboard --stop`, and the remedy paragraph now lists the stop command alongside closing the desktop app. ## Related Issue Fixes #90778 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` — `_format_venv_python_holders_message`: `serve` and `dashboard` get separate classification branches with per-branch comments; the remedy paragraph mentions `hermes dashboard --stop` - `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_venv_holders_message.py` — four regression tests: serve keeps the desktop-backend hint; dashboard is labeled standalone (and NOT desktop backend) with the stop command; gateway hint unchanged; the remedy line names both `hermes dashboard --stop` and `hermes update --force-venv` ## How to Test 1. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_venv_holders_message.py -q` — should pass (4 passed) 2. Observed result: with the update_cmd change stashed, the dashboard-classification and remedy-line tests fail (standalone dashboard inherits the desktop-backend label, no stop command anywhere); with the fix, all four pass 3. Manual equivalence: run `hermes dashboard` in one terminal and `hermes update` in another on Windows — the holder list now reads "← standalone dashboard (stop with: hermes dashboard --stop)" instead of the desktop-app advice ## Checklist - [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines - [x] Self-review completed - [x] Comments added for complex logic (why serve and dashboard are different programs) - [x] Tests added that prove the fix is effective or prevent regression (all three classifications + remedy line) - [x] All new and existing tests pass locally (4/4) - [x] Platform: macOS (pure message-formatting logic; the Windows .pyd locking behavior it explains is unchanged)

signals.title: fix(desktop): use --query-file for bot-to-bot @mention handoff instead of unsafe -q
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes #91105 — Bot-to-bot @mention messages silently dropping after v0.20.4. The composer middleware told agents to run `hermes -p <bot> chat ... -q "Message from 🤖 ..."` with the message body **inline** in a double-quoted shell argument. If the composed message contained double quotes, ``, backticks, or other shell-special characters, the command was mangled and the recipient never received the message. This PR updates **both** the protocol section (what bots read) **and** the composer middleware (the actual injected instructions) to use the safe `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` pattern already established in the reference protocol at `tools/bot_mode_probe.py`. The agent now: 1. Writes the message to `/tmp/dm.txt` with the file tool FIRST (never inline it into the command — quotes truncate it and `` would execute) 2. Then runs `hermes -p <bot> chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q --query-file /tmp/dm.txt` This eliminates the shell-injection class entirely while preserving the existing UX. ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`: Updated `messagingProtocolSection` (protocol text bots read) and the composer middleware `resolveMentionInstructions` (actual injected instructions) to use `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt`. The instruction now tells agents to write the message to a temp file first. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs`: Updated the existing quoting tests to verify the new `--query-file` approach (replaces the old `-q` argument-parsing tests with pattern-match assertions that verify the handoff note uses `--query-file` and does NOT contain `-q ""`). ## Verification - Existing test suite at `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs` was updated and passes. - Manual verification: the handoff note now contains `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` and no longer contains `-q ""`. - The `--query-file` approach is identical to the safe pattern already used in `tools/bot_mode_probe.py` (line 178).

signals.title: feat(update): add deployment-plan admission with fail-closed legacy guard
signals.text: ## Scope Adds immutable deployment-plan authority at the `hermes update` admission boundary, before the legacy updater may back up state, stop processes, fetch source, or mutate dependencies. This is an **admission/substrate slice**, not full #91277 Phase-2 physical enforcement. ## Contract - Models deployment mode, deployment kind, canonical checkout, allowed components, runtime origins, local-provisioning authority, required postconditions, target generation, and a deterministic plan digest. - Preserves both observation-only surfaces — `--check` and the existing `--plan` inventory — without requiring a mutation envelope. - Refuses in-place mutation for image-managed, externally managed, and remote-only deployments. - Requires mutable deployments to run from the canonical checkout. - Fails closed when an explicitly configured plan is missing, malformed, or contains unknown keys. - Refuses narrowed component, runtime-origin, or provisioning authority before the monolithic updater runs because that updater cannot enforce those restrictions stage by stage. - Carries the admitted plan and digest for downstream generation and receipt work. **Boundary:** stage-aware installer, bootstrap, Desktop, and updater enforcement—and the real deployment-kind E2E required by #91277—remain downstream. Until those consumers bind to the same plan, narrowed authority fails closed rather than being silently widened. ## Current-main reconciliation Rebuilt directly on observed upstream `main` `b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff` rather than merging the stale base. The reconciliation explicitly preserves #91803's `--switch-branch` contract and restores the existing observation-only `--plan` surface; a regression proves `--plan` does not accidentally enter mutation admission. ## Exact object - Head: [`99abee7d0365f4426294be0fd1045263b206d03d`](https://github.com/andrexibiza/hermes-agent/commit/99abee7d0365f4426294be0fd1045263b206d03d) - Parent: [`b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff) - Active topology: **one commit, five changed files** - Superseded heads, including `de02b35f...`, are outside active ancestry; no status is inherited from them. ## Verification Fresh exact-head CI/Docker/Nix for `99abee7d...` is required. Previous green runs belonged to retired head `de02b35f...` and are intentionally not presented as evidence for this object. ## Interlocks - #88683 — deployment-plan architecture - #91277 — fleet-update phase ordering and physical enforcement - #91283 — merged receipt and runtime-generation verification substrate - #91895 — next physical ownership/generation-fence layer, stacked on this exact head - #91803 — parked-branch target ownership preserved during current-main reconciliation - #91079 — Desktop package candidate and rollback settlement - #91559 — PID-incarnation-safe runtime observation - #88764 — secondary Desktop provisioning authority

signals.title: fix(bot-mode): send @mention handoffs via query files
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes Bot Mode's local bot-to-bot `@mention` handoff so arbitrary composed messages never enter shell parsing. The Desktop protocol and composer middleware still embedded the message body in `-q "..."`. Quotes could truncate the message, while backticks or `$()` could be interpreted by the sender's shell. Both paths now require the agent to write the complete attributed message with the file tool first, then pass that exact, shell-quoted path to `hermes ... --query-file`. The path is intentionally supplied by the file tool rather than hard-coded to `/tmp/dm.txt`: this keeps the handoff valid on Windows and prevents concurrent or multi-recipient handoffs from overwriting one shared file. ## Related Issue Fixes #91105 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` - Update `messagingProtocolSection` to require file-tool-first delivery through `--query-file`. - Update local composer `@mention` handoff instructions to use a distinct file-tool path for each recipient. - Preserve recipient quoting, canonical `Bot Chat`, `--in ~`, `--create-if-missing`, `-Q`, and background notification behavior. - Remove the obsolete inline-double-quote escape helper. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs` - Add contracts for both protocol surfaces. - Keep executable hostile title/profile and recipient-quoting regression coverage. ## How to Test 1. In Desktop Bot Mode, create two local bots (`Sender` and `Reviewer`). 2. From Sender's Bot Chat, `@reviewer` with a message containing double quotes, single quotes, backticks, and `$()`. 3. Verify Sender writes the complete attributed message through the file tool, candidate CLI exits 0 using `--query-file`, Reviewer receives the exact bytes, and the shell-substitution sentinel is not created. Automated verification on Windows 11, final SHA `adc3a361b4d28a9b4df8f60ac1bdf526ed6bf265`: ```text node --test apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs 7 passed npm run check:test:plugins 378 passed npm run typecheck passed npm run build passed pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_chat_query_file.py -q 4 passed npx playwright test e2e/mock-backend-setup.spec.ts --reporter=list 4 passed npx playwright test e2e/bot-mention-query-file.spec.ts --reporter=list 1 passed — real Electron → middleware → file tool → background terminal → candidate CLI → Reviewer backend ``` The feature E2E used a temporary deterministic mock-inference script to issue real `write_file` and `terminal` tool calls; that harness was removed after verification and is not part of this PR. It ran on pre-rebase SHA `b26473dd1`, whose production patch has the same stable patch-id (`5424a1c544b3cdf732dc216980b775607ff3d1c0`) as final SHA `adc3a361b`; after rebasing the unrelated upstream session-edit fix, focused tests, all plugin tests, typecheck, and production build were rerun on the final SHA. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 Duplicate check note: #91304 appeared after this work started. It currently includes an unrelated #89316 commit/files and a stale, much broader Desktop diff; it also hard-codes `/tmp/dm.txt`. This branch is rebased on current `main`, changes only the two #91105 files, and uses the exact path returned by the file tool for cross-platform and concurrent handoffs. Full Python `pytest tests/ -q` was not run because this is a Desktop plugin-only change. The focused CLI `--query-file` suite and all Desktop plugin/type/build/Electron gates above passed. ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A; no public API or configuration changes - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the compatibility guide — uses the file tool's exact path rather than `/tmp` - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs The Electron E2E verified the complete attributed payload reached Reviewer byte-for-byte and that the `$()` sentinel did not execute. No UI screenshots are needed for this transport-only fix.

signals.title: fix(desktop): strip routing @mention token before remote DM delivery (#91397)
signals.text: ## Summary Closes #91397. When a user @mentions a remote bot from the Desktop composer (e.g. `@default-homeserver: ping test`), `deliverRemoteRosterMentions` forwarded the raw user text verbatim into the recipient's canonical Bot Chat: ``` Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): @default-homeserver: ping test ``` Because Bot Mode agents are prompted to interpret `@<name>` in incoming messages as a bot-to-bot handoff request, the receiving agent re-interpreted the embedded mention as a handoff directive aimed at itself, attempting recursive self-delivery instead of answering the user query. ## Changes - Added `stripBotMentionTokens(text, bot)` in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` to strip the target routing `@mention` tokens (handle, name, friendly name forms) before wrapping the user text in the `Message from 🤖 ...` envelope. - Added regression test in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/remote-dm-delivery.test.mjs`.

signals.title: fix(kanban): split worker liveness and progress leases
signals.text: ## Summary Split Kanban worker liveness from deterministic progress and add fail-closed process identity for every local worker termination path. - model streaming and heartbeat commentary renew liveness, never progress - verified tool middleware and board transitions renew progress - default 45-minute no-progress lease requeues and counts failure - Linux worker identity uses `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time plus required boot ID, session ID, and process-group ID - termination proves ownership before SIGTERM and re-proves it before SIGKILL escalation - legacy, unreadable, recycled, remote, and non-session-leader identities never authorize a local signal - additive schema migration preserves existing boards without inventing historical proof - `no_progress` is propagated through CLI, gateway, dashboard, notifications, diagnostics, resume semantics, and all locales ## Safety invariants - An unproven or recycled PID receives no signal. - A worker group is signalled only when the live process still matches its immutable birth identity and is the dispatcher-owned session/group leader. - Ownership is re-verified after the SIGTERM grace period before any SIGKILL. - Missing Linux boot identity fails closed rather than degrading to start-time-only matching. - Refused reclamation keeps the claim visible and emits `reclaim_deferred`; it does not silently start a duplicate worker. ## Verification - targeted canonical runner: 145/145 passed - independent expanded target set: 163 passed - canonical broad comparison: 3,160 files; zero new failures versus `origin/main` - real unrelated three-process `setsid` tree: zero signals; all processes survived - genuine dispatcher-owned three-process tree: fully reaped - escalation-window PID replacement: initial proven SIGTERM only; zero SIGKILL/`killpg` to replacement - missing/empty/unreadable boot ID and post-reboot aliases: refused - nine mutation checks killed by committed tests - changed desktop TypeScript files: eslint passed - low-uptime limiter regression: an `Optional[float]` sentinel admits the first liveness/progress event at monotonic uptime `0.0`, `1.0`, and interval-minus-epsilon, while the second event remains rate-limited - PID identity proof: live PID, persisted PID on SID-less identities, and stored/live SID/PGID comparisons are pinned independently so no defense-in-depth leg can be removed as “redundant” - import-time limiter defaults are tested in a fresh subprocess, preventing a declaration-only regression back to the numeric sentinel ## Known verification boundary Full desktop TypeScript typecheck could not be run because the repository's `min-release-age=14` supply-chain policy correctly blocks installation of a newly published dependency. The policy was not bypassed. The edited TypeScript is additive notifier/i18n mapping code and passed changed-file eslint. ## Deployment This PR only publishes the reviewed source. No live board, database, dispatcher, or Hermes runtime was modified or deployed.

signals.title: feat(desktop): right-click file artifacts for 'Open Containing Folder'
signals.text: ## Summary of Changes <!-- What does this PR do, and why? What problem does it solve? --> Chat file artifacts had no right-click menu, so there was no way to get to a file's folder except through the file-browser sidebar. This adds a context menu to: - the "Open `<file>`" fallback link (non-media `MEDIA:` attachments, e.g. a PDF named in a message), and - inline markdown images The menu offers **Reveal in File Explorer** (macOS: Reveal in Finder) + **Copy Path**. ### Implementation - New shared component `src/components/chat/reveal-in-folder.tsx` (`RevealInFolderTrigger`) — one ContextMenu reused by both surfaces, keeping the two files from importing each other. - Reuses the existing `revealDesktopPath` → `hermes:fs:reveal` IPC (`shell.showItemInFolder`) and the existing `fileMenu` i18n wording via `pickRevealLabel` — identical label/behavior to the file-browser trees, zero new i18n keys. - `navigator.clipboard.writeText` for Copy Path (already shimmed to IPC app-wide). - **Local gateway only:** when `isDesktopFsRemoteMode()` is true the file lives on the gateway machine, so the menu is hidden — same gating the file trees use. - `rawSrc` (the original disk path) is threaded through `MarkdownImage`/`MarkdownImageContent` into `ZoomableImage` as `revealPath`, so reveal targets the real file, not a `blob:` URL. - `MarkdownTextContent` now exposes its `notify`/`notifyError` handlers (needed by the shared component) — no behavior change for consumers that don't pass them. ## Linked Issues <!-- Does this fix a specific issue? Use "Fixes #123" to auto-link --> No linked issue — user-requested enhancement. ## Related PRs <!-- Any PRs that depend on this one, or that this one depends on --> None. ## Type of Change - [x] New feature - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes) - [ ] CI/build changes - [ ] Dependency updates ## Affected Platforms - [x] Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux) - [ ] Gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix) - [ ] CLI - [ ] API - [ ] Documentation/website - [ ] Core/runtime - [ ] Not sure / multiple ## Testing Performed - [x] Typecheck: `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` in `apps/desktop` — 0 errors - [x] Lint: `npx eslint` on all four touched files — clean - [x] Tests: `npx vitest run --project ui` on `markdown-text.reveal-menu.test.tsx` (new), `markdown-text.filelinks`, `markdown-text.media`, `markdown-text.media-md` — 4 files / 12 tests, all pass (`zoomable-image` has no dedicated test file in the repo; it is covered by the typecheck and by the markdown-text media suites) **Platform tested on:** Windows **Verified against:** `upstream/main` at `b2c4f1f376` — the three pre-existing touched files are untouched between the local dev base (`f43eabee`) and that commit, and `revealDesktopPath` / `isDesktopFsRemoteMode` signatures are unchanged, so no re-merge is needed. **Model tested with:** N/A (UI-only change) **Gateway tested with:** local ## Screenshots or Demo <!-- Include screenshots for UI changes, or a short demo/GIF if it helps reviewers --> Before: right-clicking the "Open report.pdf" link did nothing. After: right-click → **Reveal in File Explorer** opens Explorer on the file's folder with the file selected; **Copy Path** copies the absolute path. Same menu on inline images. ## Additional Context <!-- Anything else reviewers should know. Design decisions, trade-offs, follow-up work. --> - Verified clean against `upstream/main` at `b2c4f1f376`: the 3 touched files are untouched between the author's local base and that commit, and `revealDesktopPath`/`isDesktopFsRemoteMode` signatures are unchanged. - `ZoomableImage` renders the lightbox `<Dialog>` as a sibling portal outside the trigger (Radix `asChild` requires a single-element child); `lightboxOpen` state lifted to keep that wiring. - If this lands, the natural follow-up is wiring the same trigger into `preview-attachment.tsx`'s preview chrome for parity — deliberately left out to keep this diff small.

signals.title: fix(desktop): stop simple-git custom-binary warning spam on Windows
signals.text: ## Summary Supersedes stale/conflicting #79250 while preserving @hernanda-git's exact implementation and Git authorship. Hermes Desktop resolves Git from trusted process-local locations. On Windows that is normally `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`, so `gitFor()` must opt into simple-git's `unsafe.allowUnsafeCustomBinary` escape hatch. Simple-git emits the same warning on every client construction even when that opt-in is deliberate; the coding/review rail builds clients repeatedly, flooding the terminal and burying real Desktop errors. This change suppresses only the known custom-binary warning, only during the synchronous `simpleGit()` construction call, and restores `console.warn` in `finally`. Every unrelated warning remains visible. ## Field reproduction A real Windows packaged-app receipt showed the message repeated continuously: ```text Invalid value supplied for custom binary, restricted characters must be removed or supply the unsafe.allowUnsafeCustomBinary option ``` The same receipt also contains genuine ENOENT/API/network failures in the same stream. This PR removes the deterministic noise source without suppressing those independent errors. ## Provenance The original #79250 commit by @hernanda-git was replayed through GitHub onto exact upstream `main` at `ac8dff4fbcf47a392a3cddcbec068aa05930ab47`; the rebased commit retains the original Git author: - [`e90dc2a747d03e124f74b6e41f481d5f296f5119`](https://github.com/andrexibiza/hermes-agent/commit/e90dc2a747d03e124f74b6e41f481d5f296f5119) ## Tests The focused tests prove: - repeated construction through a spaced Windows Git path emits zero copies of the known warning; - `console.warn` is restored immediately, so unrelated warnings still surface; - the existing real Git-through-spaced-path contract remains intact. ## Exact-head verification All required hosted workflows attached directly to `e90dc2a747d03e124f74b6e41f481d5f296f5119` are green: - [CI 32523118643](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32523118643) — success - [Docker 32523118040](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32523118040) — success - [Nix 32523117979](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32523117979) — success GitHub currently reports the PR mergeable, rebaseable, and `mergeable_state: clean`. No status is inherited from #79250 or an adjacent object.

Fixes #90778 and #87594; empirically verifies #78089 is already fixed. Part of the #91277 venv-holder consolidation. ## Evidence-driven scope An on-demand Windows lane (fires ONLY on `wine2e/**` branches — inert on PRs/main) ran the probe suite against unfixed main first: #90778 reproduced live (both the `hermes dashboard` mislabel and `--preserve-cache` matching "serve"), #87594 reproduced live (scan returned `pids: []` under a gateway parent), #78089 passed (already fixed on main — issue can be closed). ## Changes - `_hermes_holder_subcommand()` (#90778): token-based parse of the actual Hermes subcommand — profile selectors skipped, flags never matched, unknown argv gets NO hint instead of a wrong one. signals.title: fix(codex): apply cross-issuer reasoning guard to auxiliary Responses calls
signals.text: ## Summary - Closes #91886 — the cross-issuer `encrypted_content` guard in `_chat_messages_to_responses_input()` only ran on the main-turn transport (`agent/transports/codex.py`); the auxiliary call path (`agent/auxiliary_client.py::_CodexCompletionsAdapter`, used by context compression, `flush_memories`, and MoA aggregation) never classified its own endpoint, so `current_issuer_kind` stayed `None` and the guard was inert there. - A session whose main turn runs on one Responses issuer (e.g. ChatGPT Codex OAuth) while `auxiliary.<task>` targets a different issuer (xAI, GitHub Copilot Responses, another Codex account) would replay a foreign-issued `encrypted_content` reasoning blob on the next auxiliary call and get a non-retryable `HTTP 400 invalid_encrypted_content`, breaking that background call. - Fix: classify the auxiliary client's own endpoint the same way the main transport does (`_classify_responses_issuer`) and pass it through as `current_issuer_kind`. No change to the shared converter or the main transport; purely additive on the auxiliary path, no behavior change for same-issuer sessions. ## Diagram ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'dark', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#00f0ff', 'mainBkg': '#0a0a16', 'primaryTextColor': '#ffffff', 'primaryBorderColor': '#ff007f', 'lineColor': '#00f0ff'}}}%% graph TD A[🔒 Session history] -->|codex_reasoning_items encrypted_content| B{Which call path?} B -->|⚡ Main turn| C[agent/transports/codex.py] B -->|⚡ Auxiliary call| D[agent/auxiliary_client.py] C -->|classifies own issuer| E[_classify_responses_issuer] D -.->|BEFORE: no classification| F[current_issuer_kind = None] D -->|AFTER: classifies own issuer too| E E --> G[_chat_messages_to_responses_input guard] F -->|guard inert| H[🩸 foreign blob replayed] G -->|foreign issuer dropped| I[🚀 same-issuer blob replayed OK] H --> J[❌ HTTP 400 invalid_encrypted_content] I --> K[✅ auxiliary call succeeds] ``` ## Test plan - [x] New regression tests: `TestAuxiliaryCrossIssuerReasoningGuard::test_drops_reasoning_minted_by_a_different_issuer`, `::test_keeps_reasoning_minted_by_the_same_issuer` - [x] `pytest tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py` — 184 passed - [x] `pytest tests/agent/test_codex_responses_adapter.py` — 16 passed - [x] Manual PoC reproducing the leak pre-fix (0 foreign items sent post-fix vs 1 before)

signals.title: feat(update): enforce generation-fenced deployment transaction authority
signals.text: ## Scope Implements the next physical-enforcement layer below #91316's deployment-plan admission. This is deliberately **deployment-specific**, not a repository-wide mutation wrapper: one `hermes update` mutation receives one durable authority object bound to the exact admitted plan, canonical checkout, pre-mutation generation, optional target generation, and operation ID. ## Invariant > A deployment mutation may settle its source boundary only if the authority admitted before mutation is still the durable owner at settlement and the committed source generation is observed at the exact admitted deployment root. That closes the compatibility-layer gap between "the plan allowed this update" and "the object actually mutated under that authority." It does **not** claim stage-level, process-level, or fleet-wide completion proof that the legacy monolithic updater cannot yet provide. ## Implementation - Adds `DeploymentMutationPermit` carrying plan digest, canonical checkout, admitted generation, optional target generation, operation ID, issue time, and deterministic permit digest. - Acquires one durable per-deployment update owner with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`; overlapping updater mutations fail closed. - Re-reads the durable token before generation observation and immediately before release, so an in-memory caller cannot self-certify after its ownership object has been replaced. - Persists scoped settled/aborted source-boundary evidence and fsyncs file + containing directory where supported. - Requires an explicitly authorized `target_generation` to equal the generation actually present at settlement. - Wraps the existing monolithic updater under this authority without pretending it has stage-level proof. - Preserves both observation-only `--check` and `--plan`, plus #91803's `--switch-branch` contract inherited through the reconciled #91316 parent. - Adds focused regressions for overlapping ownership, post-admission authority replacement, target-generation mismatch, settlement evidence, false-success prevention, and permit continuity across the mutation. ## Topology / interlocks Primary implementation lane: - #88683 — transactional install/update/bootstrap architecture - #91277 — Phase-2 deployment-plan tracker - #91316 — prerequisite admission/substrate; this PR is stacked on exact head `99abee7d0365f4426294be0fd1045263b206d03d` Architecture laws consumed, not duplicated: - #90144 — proof scope must equal mutation scope - #90145 — teardown/recovery fenced by durable generation identity - #90049 — typed completion proof / false-success class - #90150 — delivered artifact/process realization belongs in proof - #90866 — qualified identity + generation + proof scope + typed completion survive to the side effect Adjacent concrete implementations: - #91803 — parked-branch target ownership - #91079 — Desktop rollback/candidate transaction - #91559 — PID-incarnation-safe runtime observation ## Boundary This PR establishes the **source/deployment mutation authority** for the legacy updater. It intentionally does not declare the full #91277 Phase-2 fleet transaction complete: process replacement, per-stage component permits, exact physical-root incarnation, and post-relaunch generation handshakes still need to consume/extend this authority before the deployment can carry a full typed completion proof. ## Exact object - Head: [`6b5e0fa3319f9ce7570484cca9f60dc5181ad8d4`](https://github.com/andrexibiza/hermes-agent/commit/6b5e0fa3319f9ce7570484cca9f60dc5181ad8d4) - Parent/prerequisite: #91316 head [`99abee7d0365f4426294be0fd1045263b206d03d`](https://github.com/andrexibiza/hermes-agent/commit/99abee7d0365f4426294be0fd1045263b206d03d) - #91316 is itself rebuilt directly on observed upstream `main` `b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff` - Active implementation delta over #91316: **one commit, three files** - Superseded construction heads are outside active ancestry; no checks are inherited from them. ## Verification Fresh exact-head CI/Docker/Nix for `6b5e0fa3...` is required. No prior green status is presented as evidence for this exact object. Part of #88683. Part of #91277. Depends on #91316.

signals.title: fix(deps): restack advisory remediation on current main
signals.text: ## Priority **P0 dependency-security remediation — draft / generation object only.** Current `main` still carries the dependency-security graph this campaign is intended to replace. This is a remediation-priority statement, not a claim of active exploitation. ## Current source of truth Exact upstream `main`: `b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff`. Live PR head: `c35060427bbd1011604502e9d4a4a2121e03a500`. The branch was temporarily advanced through publication experiments and has now been restored to this staging/generation object. The submitted tree is still only the generator/publication mechanism: **6 commits, 2 changed files** (`.github/scripts/restack_dependency_security.py` and `.github/workflows/restack-dependency-security.yml`). The generated dependency graph is not the PR branch tree, so this object remains draft and is not merge-authorized. ## Exact live-head runs Latest runs for `c35060427bbd1011604502e9d4a4a2121e03a500`: - Restack dependency-security remediation [`32544350298`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32544350298) — **success** - Docker [`32544350302`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32544350302) — **success** - Nix [`32544350262`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32544350262) — **success** - CI [`32544350846`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32544350846) — **failure** No predecessor green is inherited for the live head. ## Generated remediation graph Successful restack runs have generated and verified the intended current-main-composed dependency graph. The generated payload is eight files: - `.npmrc` - `package.json` - `package-lock.json` - `uv.lock` - `apps/desktop/package.json` - `apps/desktop/scripts/packaged-app-layout.mjs` - `apps/desktop/scripts/packaged-app-layout.test.mjs` - `apps/desktop/scripts/test-desktop.mjs` The verified graph composes Electron/build pin `41.10.3`, removal of the legacy Electron extractor edge, scoped PostCSS → Nano ID `3.3.18` while Nano ID 6 stays `6.0.0`, `h2==4.4.1`, current-main React Compiler movement, and x64/ARM64 packaged-layout behavior. The original exact generated artifact for this head is `dependency-security-restack-c35060427bbd1011604502e9d4a4a2121e03a500` (artifact id `9466562504`, digest `sha256:07aedf0aaed46546dd4bfb9fa9cb29cecf5d533bd8cefe4df4dd37e389e51ff3`) from run [`32539589972`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32539589972). Those bytes are generation evidence only, not branch-tree authority. ## Publication boundary Publication was attempted through reversible repository-authorized paths, including trusted-fork workflow changes. Fresh source-of-truth read-back shows the branch restored to `c350604...`; the generated eight-file payload still did not become the submitted PR tree. The remaining hard boundary is byte-exact publication of that generated payload—especially the two ~720 KiB canonical lockfiles—onto the PR branch, followed by fresh exact-final-head CI/Docker/Nix/OSV. The available GitHub mutation surface can create blobs from inline text but has no artifact/file-reference-to-blob bridge; the local execution environment cannot use direct git/GitHub network access. Hand-editing or substituting a historical lock graph would violate the exact-object contract. ## Provenance / surviving ownership This is a restack, not independent rediscovery: - #89479 by @schmitzi8 is the primary source for Electron `41.10.3`, the internal extractor transition, and Linux ARM64 packaged-layout repair/test. - #90486 by @orcaspainting-dev supplies the scoped PostCSS → Nano ID `3.3.18` override that preserves Nano ID 6 consumers. - #91042 preserves historical combined remediation/evidence chronology but is closed unmerged with no surviving delivery diff. - #91230 is the exact-object architecture interlock: historical verification is not active delivery state. The final implementation commit must preserve contributor credit for @schmitzi8 and @orcaspainting-dev. ## Final acceptance contract Do not mark ready until the generated payload is the actual PR head and that exact object proves current-main dependency preservation, Electron/build `41.10.3`, removal of the legacy extractor edge, Nano ID `3.3.18`/`6.0.0` split, `h2==4.4.1`, `uv lock --check`, packaged-layout regression, clean High/Critical audits, removal of temporary generation files, and green CI/Docker/Nix/OSV on the exact final head.

signals.title: feat(bot-mode): @mentions identify who you mean — the agent composes and sends, the renderer never delivers
signals.text: ## Summary The Desktop @mention middleware now only *identifies* — it resolves the user's @tags against the live Bot Mode roster and tells the active agent exactly who is meant (profile, friendly name, device); the agent decides and messages through its own `message_agent` tool. The renderer's parallel delivery transport is deleted, so no path anywhere forwards user text verbatim or teaches shellouts. This finishes the class the `message_agent` merge (#91802) opened: the middleware was never meant to be a transport — it was supposed to be a picking/identification aid (autocomplete + "this @tag means this bot"), with all messaging owned by the agent. Closes the premises behind #91397 (verbatim routing-token forwarding to remote bots) and #91304 (shellout quoting in the injected handoff command) at the source. ## Changes - `plugin.js` (−553 net): mention middleware rewritten to emit an identification note (`@dixie = agent profile "dixie" ("Ops Bot") — on Mac Mini`) + a compose-and-use-message_agent instruction; deleted `deliverRemoteRosterMentions`, `pollRemoteDmReply`, `ensureRemoteCanonicalChat`, `REMOTE_DM_*`, the `[@mention handoff — hermes -p …]` and "Desktop is delivering over Connections" instruction blocks, and the now-orphaned `shellDoubleQuote`. Composer @-autocomplete untouched. - Tests: `mention-identification.test.mjs` (7 tests) replaces `mention-handoff-quoting` + `remote-dm-delivery`; `hide-bots` and `mention-roster-cache-key` harnesses re-pinned to the new contract. - `website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md`: @mentions section describes identification + agent-owned sending; cross-machine reach points at `hermes peer`. ## Behavior notes - A mention in a session without `message_agent` (regular chats) is still identified; the note tells the agent to say agent messaging is unavailable there rather than improvise a transport. - Cross-machine DMs go through registered peer gateways (`message_agent target="peer/agent"`), not a renderer side-channel. ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | hermes-bots plugin suite | 390/390 pass | | Sabotage run (renderer delivery call re-added) | 2 containment tests fail; restored → green | | Poisoned bot title | inert prose — no shell context exists to break out of | | Source contract | pins deletion of all transport symbols + both instruction blocks | Closes #91397, closes #91304 — both premises are structurally gone; thanks @loulanyue and @JinUltimate1995 for surfacing the class. ## Infographic ![Mentions point, agents speak](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa749ee/Wzy1Q8iOzurIbVBvhTUA5_bxMkLI3g.png)

signals.title: refactor(bot-mode): add shadow control-plane contracts
signals.text: ## Summary Introduces Phase 1 of #91911: one typed, shadow-only seam for Bot Mode identity, effective runtime/capability, policy decisions, and legacy parity. - add exact source-qualified `BotAddress`; - add immutable per-turn `BotExecutionContext`; - add `RuntimeCapabilitySnapshot` bound to the complete four-axis address; - add structured `BotPolicyDecision` and stable reason codes; - fail closed on address, profile-revision, grant, revocation-epoch, runtime-snapshot, or capability mismatch; - keep legacy authorization authoritative through `ShadowPolicyComparison`; - map the current #91802 `message_agent` injection and dispatch gates exactly; and - prove the typed mapping against the live implementation, including its current asymmetries. This PR has **no production imports or call sites and no behavior change**. The new policy layer cannot grant or deny work. A shadow comparison's effective result is always the legacy result until a later boundary-migration PR explicitly switches authority and deletes the superseded gate. ## Root cause Bot Mode currently derives identity and authority independently from profile names, canonical `Bot Chat` titles, gateway routes, Desktop connection state, session-store placement, provider/model state, tool/MCP configuration, completion ownership, and local/peer delivery. Those coordinates locate a candidate actor. They do not prove that the current turn owns the profile, generation, credential, or side effect. Adding more local checks would preserve the split-brain class rather than close it. The invariant established here is: > Coordinates select. Current proof objects authorize. ## Changes ### `agent/bot_control_plane.py` Adds pure-stdlib, immutable contracts: - `BotAddress(install_id, gateway_instance_id, connection_id, profile_id)`; - `BotExecutionContext`, binding profile revision, session/turn/task, authenticated source, runtime/grant generation, cancellation scope, budget, trace, and causal identity; - `RuntimeCapabilitySnapshot`, carrying the exact `BotAddress`, effective provider/model/API mode, and revocable capability grant; - stable capability classes for local/network access, external/peer messaging, process spawn, credential use, profile configuration, and destructive work; - `evaluate_capability()`, which rejects a mismatch on **any** address axis—install, gateway instance, connection, or profile—before checking later generations; and - `ShadowPolicyComparison`, whose `effective_allowed` remains legacy-owned. No prompt text, display name, session title, environment variable, or provider label can manufacture a capability. ### Exact current `message_agent` mapping The PR records current behavior rather than silently fixing it: **Injection (`ensure_message_agent_tool`)** 1. disabled protocol denies; 2. an already-present schema allows before title/install revalidation; 3. otherwise exact `Bot Chat` title is required; 4. then a Bot-Mode-managed install is required. **Dispatch (`message_agent_tool`)** 1. exact `Bot Chat` title is required; 2. a Bot-Mode-managed install is required; 3. protocol toggle and schema presence are not consulted. `LegacyMessageAgentState` and the two mapping functions preserve those orderings as evidence. They do not become a second authority. ### Tests - owner-level tests cover strict four-axis identity, immutability, capability normalization, prompt-shaped fake grants, exact-generation allow, and fail-closed mismatch outcomes; - an axis-by-axis matrix proves that changing only the install, gateway instance, connection, or profile invalidates the grant; - shadow tests prove disagreement is measurable but cannot change legacy behavior; and - live parity tests import `tools.bot_mode_dm` and compare the typed mapping against the current injection and dispatch gates, including the schema-present injection early return and dispatch's protocol-toggle asymmetry. ### Design record `docs/design/bot-mode-control-plane.md` defines the contracts, rollout order, contributor interlocks, acceptance invariants, and explicit non-goals. Existing contributor objects remain the implementation owners of their behavior: #91802, #90329, #89455, #90954, #91889, #91862, #88819, #91832, and #73923. ## Verification Prepared from exact upstream object: ```text NousResearch/hermes-agent@b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff ``` Local pure-contract validation on the exact published file objects: ```text python -m pytest tests/agent/test_bot_control_plane.py -q 34 passed python -m compileall -q agent tests passed ``` Published range verification: ```text status: ahead behind: 0 commits: 7 files: 4 added, 0 modified, 0 deleted head: d8a5fc14d06d3503dd0ca472189d3a683c755c60 ``` The full-repository `message_agent` parity file is included in the pushed head; GitHub Actions is authoritative for that integrated import path and the repository-wide lint/test matrix. ## Risk Low and deliberately bounded: - four new files only; - no production import; - no runtime I/O; - no transport, provider, profile, Desktop, or schema mutation; - no switch from legacy authority; and - no exactly-once delivery claim. ## Follow-up boundary The next slice should construct these objects at authenticated gateway ingress and compare exactly one consuming boundary in shadow mode, emitting only bounded content-free mismatch evidence. It must still leave legacy behavior authoritative. Refs #91911 Refs #91802
