signal.title: Bot-to-bot @mention messages silently drop after v0.20.4 update (composer middleware still uses unsafe -q instead of --query-file)
signal.text: ## Summary Bot-to-bot `@mention` messages silently drop after the v0.20.4 desktop update (commit `4a5b6dd45`). The sender bot's composer middleware tells it to run `hermes -p <recipient> chat ... -q "Message from 🤖 ..."` but the message body is embedded directly in the shell command via `-q "..."`. If the composed message contains double quotes, `$()`, backticks, or other shell-special characters, the command is mangled and the recipient never receives the message. The `tools/bot_mode_probe.py` reference protocol was already updated to use `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` (safe for arbitrary text), but the desktop composer middleware in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` was **not** updated to match — both the protocol section shown to bots (line ~5005) and the composer middleware that injects instructions into the sender's prompt (line ~10853) still generate `-q "..."` inline. ## Symptoms - Sender bot reports "messaged @recipient" but recipient sees nothing - Retrying the same workflow sometimes works (non-deterministic — depends on whether the composed message contains shell-breaking characters) - One bot attempted to notify a downstream bot before the reviewer had finished approving — likely a partial/malformed message being misinterpreted - Started immediately after the v0.20.4 desktop update today (2026-08-20) ## Root cause Inconsistent delivery protocol between the reference implementation and the actual composer middleware: | Location | Mechanism | |----------|-----------| | `tools/bot_mode_probe.py` (reference) | `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` ✅ | | `plugin.js` protocol section (bots read this) | `-q "..."` ❌ | | `plugin.js` composer middleware (actual delivery) | `-q "..."` ❌ | The `-q "..."` approach is fundamentally unsafe for arbitrary bot-composed text. The `--query-file` approach writes to a temp file first and is safe. ## Fix Update `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` to use `--query-file` in both places: 1. The `messagingProtocolSection` function (the protocol text bots are instructed to follow) 2. The composer middleware `resolveMentionInstructions` (the actual injected instructions) Both should match the `--query-file` approach already in `bot_mode_probe.py`. ## Version - hermes-agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), commit `4a5b6dd45` - Desktop: macOS - Host: macOS (Mac mini, M1) 🤖 This issue was filed by Hermes desktop (hermes-doctor-triage) on behalf of the user.
signal.author: piskooooo

signal.title: fix(bot-mode): send @mention handoffs via query files
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes Bot Mode's local bot-to-bot `@mention` handoff so arbitrary composed messages never enter shell parsing. The Desktop protocol and composer middleware still embedded the message body in `-q "..."`. Quotes could truncate the message, while backticks or `$()` could be interpreted by the sender's shell. Both paths now require the agent to write the complete attributed message with the file tool first, then pass that exact, shell-quoted path to `hermes ... --query-file`. The path is intentionally supplied by the file tool rather than hard-coded to `/tmp/dm.txt`: this keeps the handoff valid on Windows and prevents concurrent or multi-recipient handoffs from overwriting one shared file. ## Related Issue Fixes #91105 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` - Update `messagingProtocolSection` to require file-tool-first delivery through `--query-file`. - Update local composer `@mention` handoff instructions to use a distinct file-tool path for each recipient. - Preserve recipient quoting, canonical `Bot Chat`, `--in ~`, `--create-if-missing`, `-Q`, and background notification behavior. - Remove the obsolete inline-double-quote escape helper. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs` - Add contracts for both protocol surfaces. - Keep executable hostile title/profile and recipient-quoting regression coverage. ## How to Test 1. In Desktop Bot Mode, create two local bots (`Sender` and `Reviewer`). 2. From Sender's Bot Chat, `@reviewer` with a message containing double quotes, single quotes, backticks, and `$()`. 3. Verify Sender writes the complete attributed message through the file tool, candidate CLI exits 0 using `--query-file`, Reviewer receives the exact bytes, and the shell-substitution sentinel is not created. Automated verification on Windows 11, final SHA `adc3a361b4d28a9b4df8f60ac1bdf526ed6bf265`: ```text node --test apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs 7 passed npm run check:test:plugins 378 passed npm run typecheck passed npm run build passed pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_chat_query_file.py -q 4 passed npx playwright test e2e/mock-backend-setup.spec.ts --reporter=list 4 passed npx playwright test e2e/bot-mention-query-file.spec.ts --reporter=list 1 passed — real Electron → middleware → file tool → background terminal → candidate CLI → Reviewer backend ``` The feature E2E used a temporary deterministic mock-inference script to issue real `write_file` and `terminal` tool calls; that harness was removed after verification and is not part of this PR. It ran on pre-rebase SHA `b26473dd1`, whose production patch has the same stable patch-id (`5424a1c544b3cdf732dc216980b775607ff3d1c0`) as final SHA `adc3a361b`; after rebasing the unrelated upstream session-edit fix, focused tests, all plugin tests, typecheck, and production build were rerun on the final SHA. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 Duplicate check note: #91304 appeared after this work started. It currently includes an unrelated #89316 commit/files and a stale, much broader Desktop diff; it also hard-codes `/tmp/dm.txt`. This branch is rebased on current `main`, changes only the two #91105 files, and uses the exact path returned by the file tool for cross-platform and concurrent handoffs. Full Python `pytest tests/ -q` was not run because this is a Desktop plugin-only change. The focused CLI `--query-file` suite and all Desktop plugin/type/build/Electron gates above passed. ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A; no public API or configuration changes - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the compatibility guide — uses the file tool's exact path rather than `/tmp` - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs The Electron E2E verified the complete attributed payload reached Reviewer byte-for-byte and that the `$()` sentinel did not execute. No UI screenshots are needed for this transport-only fix.

signal.title: fix(desktop): surface actionable error when Nous Cloud agent returns 503 (#85335)
signal.text: ## Fix for #85335 ### Problem When Hermes Desktop connects to a Nous-managed cloud agent (e.g. `https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com`) and that backend returns **HTTP 502/503/504**, the error surfaced as a generic "Hermes backend did not become ready" message with no guidance that the cloud server itself is down — and the app appeared stuck in a retry loop. The user cannot restart a Nous-managed cloud instance themselves and had no actionable recovery path. ### Fix (whole class, all failure boundaries) Classifies a Nous Cloud **502/503/504** server-side fault at **every** startup boundary, carries a structured signal to the renderer, and renders an actionable recovery screen. Not just the one site the report hit: - **`backend-health.ts`** — `isServerSideHttpError` (structured-first on `err.statusCode`, legacy `^NNN:` prefix as fallback, non-`Error` inputs rejected), `isNousCloudAgentUrl`, and a single `makeNousCloudBackendDownError` factory. Used in `waitForHermesReady` (readiness exhaustion). - **`main.ts`** — runs the Cloud classifier at the **OAuth WS-ticket mint boundary** (`mintGatewayWsTicket`) before the `gatewayTicketFailure` wrap, so a Cloud 503 from the ticket endpoint surfaces the actionable message instead of the generic reachability error. 401/403 still route to reauth. Also carries `isCloudBackendDown` / `statusCode` through `DesktopBootProgress` so the renderer can key on the structured result. - **`connection-config.ts`** — `gatewayTicketFailure` preserves the source error's integer `statusCode` (401/403 → reauth, unchanged). - **`global.d.ts`** — `DesktopBootProgress` gains `isCloudBackendDown?` / `statusCode?`. - **`boot-failure-overlay.tsx`** — the recovery screen now branches on `isCloudBackendDown`: cloud-specific title/description, local-only **Repair dropped**, and the actionable portal / Local-mode / Discord guidance. The electron factory's full message is still shown in the error box. - **i18n** — `cloudDownTitle/Description/Hint` keys (en + ar/ja/zh/zh-hant). The actionable message a user now sees: names the failing cloud host, reports the HTTP status, points to https://portal.nousresearch.com, offers switching to Local mode, and gives the Discord support link. ### Tests - `backend-health.test.ts` — 502/503/504 structured + legacy + non-Error rejection, cloud-wrap on readiness exhaustion, non-cloud 503 not wrapped, factory shape/cause/guards. - `connection-config.test.ts` — OAuth ticket-mint **503 → transport failure with `statusCode` preserved**; **401 → reauth (never Cloud-down)**; integer-only statusCode copy. - `boot-failure-overlay.test.tsx` — cloud-down recovery renders, Repair dropped, portal guidance shown (4/4 passing). - TypeScript: `tsc --noEmit` clean across the desktop project (0 errors). ### Verification - Renderer overlay suite: 4/4 passing. - Electron suites: present but the vitest runner hangs in this environment (documented limitation); verified via the same direct-execution path the author used. Fixes #85335 Related (same debugging session, separate class): #85333 (read_file dedup) via #85353.

signal.title: feat(bot-mode): @mentions identify who you mean — the agent composes and sends, the renderer never delivers
signal.text: ## Summary The Desktop @mention middleware now only *identifies* — it resolves the user's @tags against the live Bot Mode roster and tells the active agent exactly who is meant (profile, friendly name, device); the agent decides and messages through its own `message_agent` tool. The renderer's parallel delivery transport is deleted, so no path anywhere forwards user text verbatim or teaches shellouts. This finishes the class the `message_agent` merge (#91802) opened: the middleware was never meant to be a transport — it was supposed to be a picking/identification aid (autocomplete + "this @tag means this bot"), with all messaging owned by the agent. Closes the premises behind #91397 (verbatim routing-token forwarding to remote bots) and #91304 (shellout quoting in the injected handoff command) at the source. ## Changes - `plugin.js` (−553 net): mention middleware rewritten to emit an identification note (`@dixie = agent profile "dixie" ("Ops Bot") — on Mac Mini`) + a compose-and-use-message_agent instruction; deleted `deliverRemoteRosterMentions`, `pollRemoteDmReply`, `ensureRemoteCanonicalChat`, `REMOTE_DM_*`, the `[@mention handoff — hermes -p …]` and "Desktop is delivering over Connections" instruction blocks, and the now-orphaned `shellDoubleQuote`. Composer @-autocomplete untouched. - Tests: `mention-identification.test.mjs` (7 tests) replaces `mention-handoff-quoting` + `remote-dm-delivery`; `hide-bots` and `mention-roster-cache-key` harnesses re-pinned to the new contract. - `website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md`: @mentions section describes identification + agent-owned sending; cross-machine reach points at `hermes peer`. ## Behavior notes - A mention in a session without `message_agent` (regular chats) is still identified; the note tells the agent to say agent messaging is unavailable there rather than improvise a transport. - Cross-machine DMs go through registered peer gateways (`message_agent target="peer/agent"`), not a renderer side-channel. ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | hermes-bots plugin suite | 390/390 pass | | Sabotage run (renderer delivery call re-added) | 2 containment tests fail; restored → green | | Poisoned bot title | inert prose — no shell context exists to break out of | | Source contract | pins deletion of all transport symbols + both instruction blocks | Closes #91397, closes #91304 — both premises are structurally gone; thanks @loulanyue and @JinUltimate1995 for surfacing the class. ## Infographic ![Mentions point, agents speak](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa749ee/Wzy1Q8iOzurIbVBvhTUA5_bxMkLI3g.png)

signal.title: [Bug]: fix(desktop) remote @mention delivery forwards the routing token in the body, so the recipient re-routes instead of answering
signal.text: --- name: "🐛 Bug Report" about: Remote @mention delivery forwards the routing token in the body, so the recipient re-routes instead of answering title: "fix(desktop): remote @mention delivery forwards the routing token in the body, so the recipient re-routes instead of answering" labels: ["bug"] --- ### Bug Description When a user @mentions a **remote** bot (an agent on another Connection) from the Desktop composer, the desktop delivers the message to the remote machine **with the routing `@mention` still embedded verbatim in the body**. The receiving Bot Mode agent re-interprets that `@mention` as a *bot-to-bot handoff instruction* and tries to route the message again — instead of answering the user. This is inconsistent with the **local** bot-to-bot path, where the middleware explicitly instructs the sending agent to *compose a new message* and never forward the user's text verbatim. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Desktop connected to a remote machine over SSH (Bot Mode roster shows the remote agent, e.g. `@default-homeserver`). 2. In a normal chat with the local agent, send: `@default-homeserver ping test` 3. Desktop middleware resolves the mention and delivers over Connections. The remote "Bot Chat" session receives: ``` Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): @default-homeserver ping test ``` 4. Observe the remote agent's behavior. ### Expected Behavior The mention is **routing metadata**, consumed by the sender's middleware. Once resolved, it should not reach the recipient as live syntax. The recipient should see: ``` Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): ping test ``` …and answer it as a user-origin, pre-routed message. ### Actual Behavior The remote agent treated the embedded `@default-homeserver` in the delivered body as a **handoff request aimed at itself**: 1. Composed a follow-up and ran `hermes -p default-homeserver chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q --query-file /tmp/dm_win_ping.txt` (a recursive self-delivery attempt), 2. When that failed (the profile had just been deleted), spent its turn investigating "the recipient bot no longer exists — delivery failed", 3. Never answered the actual user question ("ping test"). Verified via the remote `state.db` — full landing record: ``` 16:43:58 | user | Message from 🤖 Win-corp (@hermes): @default-homeserver ping test 16:44:29 | tool | {"output": "Background process started", "session_id": "proc_…", …} 16:44:33 | user | [IMPORTANT: Background process proc_… exited (exit code 1). Command: hermes -p default-homeserver chat …] 16:44:47 | assistant | "@default-homeserver does not exist anymore (deleted) … delivery to the destination bot failed" ``` Impact: - Wasted turns / wrong answers on every remote mention whose body echoes the handle. - **Recursion risk**: if the mentioned handle exists on the recipient, it will happily re-dispatch, potentially chaining across machines (A → B → C) with no dedup or loop guard. - Confusing UX: user gets "delivery failed" reports about a bot they successfully reached. ### Affected Component Other — Desktop app (Bot Mode mention middleware, remote delivery over Connections) ### Messaging Platform N/A (CLI only) — this is the desktop Connections channel, not a gateway platform. ### Debug Report Not attached. `hermes debug share` was run during triage, but the uploaded bundle contains tailnet IP addresses and verbatim personal chat messages, so the links were deliberately withheld from this public report. The decisive evidence for this bug is not in those logs anyway — it is (a) the remote machine's `state.db` landing record, quoted verbatim in *Actual Behavior* above, and (b) the renderer bundle's delivery code, quoted in *Root Cause Analysis*. Full logs (redacted or raw) available on request. ### Operating System Windows 11 (sender/desktop) · macOS (receiver, over SSH Connection) ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version v0.20.4 (2026.8.18) · upstream `8e77d031` · desktop build `524b0622` (built 2026-08-21T06:24Z) ### Root Cause Analysis Two independent design gaps combine: 1. **Sender side** — the remote delivery path submits the raw user text untouched (renderer bundle, remote mention delivery): ```js prompt.submit({ session_id, text: `Message from 🤖 ${senderName} (@${handle}): ${rawUserText}` }) ``` The routing mention stays inside `${rawUserText}`. 2. **Receiver side** — Bot Mode trains agents to parse incoming text for `@name` handoff requests. The envelope above is indistinguishable from a genuine bot-to-bot handoff (same emoji, same shape), so the recipient cannot tell "user message, already routed" from "another bot asking me to relay". Note the inconsistency with the **local** path: there the middleware injects explicit instructions — *"COMPOSE a message from you to that agent conveying what the user wants — do not forward this text verbatim"* — i.e. the local path already follows exactly the principle this report asks for. Only the remote path leaks the routing token. Related (all reviewed before filing; none cover the verbatim-forwarding gap): - #91339 / #91304 — handoff quoting safety (`--query-file`); different problem (shell parsing), same subsystem. - #91359 — group @mention rendering; visual layer only. - #89710 / #91340 / #91247 / #91081 — mention resolution / roster-cache fixes, all merged before this report. ### Proposed Fix Either side suffices; both is safest: - **Sender**: strip the resolved mention token(s) from the delivered text before wrapping in the envelope. For multi-mention texts (`@a tell @b …`), keep co-mentioned targets as structured metadata rather than bare tokens. - **Receiver**: define the envelope as a distinct, recognizable format (or add an explicit marker field) and instruct Bot Mode agents that anything arriving inside a Connections envelope is **user-origin and pre-routed** — never act on `@` tokens inside the quoted body. Happy to provide additional logs or test against newer builds.

signal.title: fix(desktop): use --query-file for bot-to-bot @mention handoff instead of unsafe -q
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes #91105 — Bot-to-bot @mention messages silently dropping after v0.20.4. The composer middleware told agents to run `hermes -p <bot> chat ... -q "Message from 🤖 ..."` with the message body **inline** in a double-quoted shell argument. If the composed message contained double quotes, ``, backticks, or other shell-special characters, the command was mangled and the recipient never received the message. This PR updates **both** the protocol section (what bots read) **and** the composer middleware (the actual injected instructions) to use the safe `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` pattern already established in the reference protocol at `tools/bot_mode_probe.py`. The agent now: 1. Writes the message to `/tmp/dm.txt` with the file tool FIRST (never inline it into the command — quotes truncate it and `` would execute) 2. Then runs `hermes -p <bot> chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q --query-file /tmp/dm.txt` This eliminates the shell-injection class entirely while preserving the existing UX. ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`: Updated `messagingProtocolSection` (protocol text bots read) and the composer middleware `resolveMentionInstructions` (actual injected instructions) to use `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt`. The instruction now tells agents to write the message to a temp file first. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs`: Updated the existing quoting tests to verify the new `--query-file` approach (replaces the old `-q` argument-parsing tests with pattern-match assertions that verify the handoff note uses `--query-file` and does NOT contain `-q ""`). ## Verification - Existing test suite at `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs` was updated and passes. - Manual verification: the handoff note now contains `--query-file /tmp/dm.txt` and no longer contains `-q ""`. - The `--query-file` approach is identical to the safe pattern already used in `tools/bot_mode_probe.py` (line 178).

Follow-up commit on top converts hint-prose URLs into action buttons to match the layered error card idiom from #91493. ## Infographic ![Cloud agent down — actionable boot recovery](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa74a36/ZYZeuC68zaC8nWyk5QsNN_S4mRvvGn.png)

signal.title: Desktop: cloud agent 503/backend unreachable produces non-actionable boot-loop with opaque error
signal.text: ## Desktop: cloud agent 503/backend unreachable produces non-actionable boot-loop with opaque error ### Bug description When a Hermes Desktop is configured to connect to a Hermes Cloud agent (e.g., `https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com`) and that backend returns **HTTP 503 Service Unavailable**, the desktop enters a boot-loop with a non-actionable error message. The user sees "Connecting to remote Hermes backend" at ~24% progress, then a generic failure with no guidance that the cloud instance itself is down. ### Configuration Desktop `connection.json` (`C:\Users\andre\AppData\Roaming\Hermes\connection.json`): ```json { "mode": "local", "remote": { "url": "https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com", "authMode": "oauth" }, "profiles": {} } ``` ### Evidence 1. **Cloud agent is down**: `curl -sv https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com/api/status` returns: ``` HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable server: Fly/40bd1ce81 (2026-08-13) via: 1.1 fly.io ``` 2. **Sandbox fallback marker** (`C:\Users\andre\AppData\Roaming\Hermes\windows-sandbox-fallback.json`): ```json {"state":"fallback","reason":"boot-loop","version":"0.17.0"} ``` This marker is from the Windows Chromium sandbox recovery system (#38216) and is **unrelated** to the backend outage — it was likely from a prior GPU/renderer crash loop and remains sticky because `markerAfterSuccessfulBoot` only clears it on a successful window reveal, which never happens when the backend is unreachable. 3. **Desktop app process is running** (`Hermes.exe` PIDs: 24344, 25640, 10096, 11404, 6352) but the gateway/backend is not reachable. 4. **No gateway process locally** — the desktop connects to the Nous-managed cloud agent, not a local `hermes gateway` or `hermes serve`. ### Root cause - The desktop boot path in `startHermes()` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:8296`) classifies this as a REMOTE failure via `primaryBackendIsRemote()` (line 7551) - `resolveRemoteBackend()` (line 7502) resolves the cloud URL and calls `buildRemoteConnection()` which calls `waitForHermes()` (from `backend-health.ts`) - `waitForHermes()` probes `/api/health` and `/api/status` — both return 503 - Per `shouldLatchBackendStartFailure()` (in `backend-start-failure.ts`), remote failures do NOT latch (they stay retryable for transient errors) - The renderer's reconnect loop (`hermes:connection:revalidate` IPC handler, main.ts:9843) probes every 60s with a 3-failure limit before dropping the cached connection - Each retry hits the same 503, so the app appears stuck in a retry loop with a non-actionable error ### Why the error is opaque - The 503 from the cloud agent is a **server-side failure**, not an auth rejection (not 401/403) - `resolveRemoteBackend()` -> `buildRemoteConnection()` -> `waitForHermes()` treats this as a transient connectivity failure - The error message surfaces as something like "Hermes backend did not become ready" or similar generic timeout - There is **no user-facing guidance** telling them: - That this is a Nous-managed cloud instance they cannot restart themselves - That they should check the Nous Portal (https://portal.nousresearch.com) for management options - That they can switch to Local mode in Settings -> Gateway as a workaround - That Discord support (discord.gg/NousResearch) is the escalation path ### Recovery paths (not currently surfaced to the user) 1. **Nous Portal** — https://portal.nousresearch.com may have cloud agent management (behind a Vercel security checkpoint; must use a real browser) 2. **Wait for Fly.io auto-recovery** — the cloud instance may auto-restart 3. **Discord** — discord.gg/NousResearch — the Nous team can restart the Fly Machine 4. **Switch to Local** — Settings -> Gateway -> switch from Cloud to Local mode (spawns a local `hermes serve` backend) ### Proposed fix When a cloud-mode connection fails with HTTP 502/503/504 (server-side errors from a Nous-managed cloud instance), the desktop should surface an actionable error message that: 1. Detects that the URL is a Nous-managed cloud agent (`*.agents.nousresearch.com`) 2. Reports the HTTP status code (503) and that the backend server is down 3. Tells the user this is a Nous-managed cloud instance they cannot restart themselves 4. Suggests checking the Nous Portal, waiting for auto-recovery, or switching to Local mode 5. Provides Discord support link for escalation ### Labels type/bug, comp/desktop, area/cloud, P2 ### Current tracking Implementation is tracked in #85373. This issue remains open until the complete Nous Cloud 502/503/504 recovery path lands.

signal.title: fix(email): endpoint-scoped Gmail app-password normalization — rebuild required
signal.text: ## Current source of truth — draft / do not merge Live head: `dd1ef90b44f72cff8a63aefc207ccc5c6735af58`. The branch is **not** the endpoint-scoped credential repair described by the historical local receipts. Its live adapter still normalizes a 4×4 password shape before the authentication endpoint is authoritative, so a same-shaped non-Google credential can be mutated and mixed-provider IMAP/SMTP configurations cannot be represented safely. The branch also contains temporary repair/materializer workflow state. This PR has therefore been returned to **draft**. GitHub mergeability is not semantic authorization. ## Required contract A correct replacement must: - store the configured password exactly as supplied; - recognize only `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` with DNS-label-boundary checks; - compact the exact Google 4×4 display form only immediately before the login call for the endpoint actually being authenticated; - select IMAP and SMTP independently, including mixed-provider configurations; - use the resolved standalone SMTP host as the source of truth; and - preserve every non-matching/non-Google credential byte-for-byte, including outer whitespace. The acceptance surface is the production adapter plus standalone send, not only a helper. ## Historical reviewed object A prior local replacement was recorded as: - commit `1e96c9f25cc7e1525aec87331f71b9bf26feadc2` — not present on GitHub; - adapter blob `0162f4f010394c5ac6e42094e8485bc75c6b74ee`; - focused-test blob `eafc0c13b71d0f397d0a3e09e9df4fd579fe90d8`; - 12 focused tests passed; - 700,000 deterministic host/credential cases passed; - AST audit accounted for all seven authentication calls; - compile / `git diff --check` clean. Those identifiers are historical evidence only. The exact reviewed replacement bytes are not available in the current persistent artifact sources, and the referenced adapter blob is not resolvable from the fork. They cannot be truthfully promoted into this branch by description alone. ## Closure gate 1. Recover the exact reviewed replacement bytes **or** independently regenerate the endpoint-scoped repair from current source under the same seven-call AST audit and adversarial host/credential matrix. 2. Replace the unsafe branch implementation rather than stacking another normalization layer on it. 3. Remove temporary repair workflows and unrelated branch churn from the merge candidate. 4. Compose onto exact current `main` and obtain fresh exact-head email tests plus CI/Docker/Nix. 5. Only then mark ready and post a completion comment. This metadata change does not claim the security-sensitive code is fixed.

signal.title: fix(desktop): stop simple-git custom-binary warning spam on Windows
signal.text: ## Summary Supersedes stale/conflicting #79250 while preserving @hernanda-git's exact implementation and Git authorship. Hermes Desktop resolves Git from trusted process-local locations. On Windows that is normally `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`, so `gitFor()` must opt into simple-git's `unsafe.allowUnsafeCustomBinary` escape hatch. Simple-git emits the same warning on every client construction even when that opt-in is deliberate; the coding/review rail builds clients repeatedly, flooding the terminal and burying real Desktop errors. This change suppresses only the known custom-binary warning, only during the synchronous `simpleGit()` construction call, and restores `console.warn` in `finally`. Every unrelated warning remains visible. ## Field reproduction A real Windows packaged-app receipt showed the message repeated continuously: ```text Invalid value supplied for custom binary, restricted characters must be removed or supply the unsafe.allowUnsafeCustomBinary option ``` The same receipt also contains genuine ENOENT/API/network failures in the same stream. This PR removes the deterministic noise source without suppressing those independent errors. ## Provenance The original #79250 commit by @hernanda-git was replayed through GitHub onto exact upstream `main` at `ac8dff4fbcf47a392a3cddcbec068aa05930ab47`; the rebased commit retains the original Git author: - [`e90dc2a747d03e124f74b6e41f481d5f296f5119`](https://github.com/andrexibiza/hermes-agent/commit/e90dc2a747d03e124f74b6e41f481d5f296f5119) ## Tests The focused tests prove: - repeated construction through a spaced Windows Git path emits zero copies of the known warning; - `console.warn` is restored immediately, so unrelated warnings still surface; - the existing real Git-through-spaced-path contract remains intact. ## Exact-head verification All required hosted workflows attached directly to `e90dc2a747d03e124f74b6e41f481d5f296f5119` are green: - [CI 32523118643](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32523118643) — success - [Docker 32523118040](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32523118040) — success - [Nix 32523117979](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/32523117979) — success GitHub currently reports the PR mergeable, rebaseable, and `mergeable_state: clean`. No status is inherited from #79250 or an adjacent object.

signal.title: fix(telegram): omit topic routing from rich edits
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Keeps Telegram DM-topic tables on the rich edit path instead of silently degrading them to legacy MarkdownV2 bullet groups. `editMessageText` identifies its target with `chat_id` and `message_id`. The rich finalize path was also forwarding `message_thread_id` or `direct_messages_topic_id`, even though those are send-routing fields. Telegram can reject that payload, after which `_try_edit_rich()` returns `None` and `edit_message()` runs `format_message()`, permanently rewriting the table as bullets. This removes the send-only routing fields from rich edits. Send and draft routing are unchanged. ## Related Issue Follow-up to #91847. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: omit topic-routing fields from rich `editMessageText` payloads. - `tests/gateway/test_telegram_rich_messages.py`: add a DM-topic regression that makes the old payload reject and proves the raw table stays on the rich edit path. ## How to Test 1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_telegram_rich_messages.py -q -j 4`. 2. Enable `rich_messages: true` and leave `rich_drafts: false` for Telegram. 3. In a Telegram DM topic, request a Markdown table with a blank line before it and verify the completed response remains a native table instead of becoming bullet groups. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [ ] I've tested on my platform ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A, no user-facing configuration or workflow changed - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — Telegram API payload construction is platform-independent - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs Not included. The regression test reproduces the payload rejection without publishing support artifacts.

signal.title: WhatsApp Feature Parity & Alignment Campaign — meta-issue
signal.text: # WhatsApp Feature Parity & Alignment Campaign — meta-issue **Campaign: bring Hermes's WhatsApp surface into full bloom and alignment with the official WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API and the bridge backends Hermes actually runs (whatsapp-web.js / Baileys / Business API).** Every WhatsApp issue, subissue, and PR in this tracker is interlocked here. One campaign, one canonical view, one reconciliation. ## Why this campaign - **456 open issues** touch the WhatsApp surface (search union: `whatsapp in:title,body`; 77 carry `platform/whatsapp` — measured 2026-08-05). - **388 open PRs** mention WhatsApp in title/body (search API total_count, 2026-08-05). - The adapter (`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`, **1,918 lines** @ 0577116f83) is a **multi-backend bridge**: WhatsApp Business API (Meta verification), whatsapp-web.js, Baileys. At 96% of the 2,000-line ceiling with accumulated responsibilities (backend dispatch, pairing/QR lifecycle, messaging, media, groups, secret + Windows-subprocess hygiene) it is a **god-file in waiting**. Under-ceiling rule (Axl, 2026-08-05): *"Just because it's under 2000 lines does not mean that you are not decomposing WhatsApp. Simplify so that it never has a chance of being longer than 2000 lines."* Lane S6 decomposes it NOW so the core adapter lands far under the ceiling with structural headroom. Headroom is the Ramp's job; the ceiling is not a target. - The surface is "conflicted at best": partial parameter coverage, silent drops, and a bridge lifecycle (QR pairing, reconnects, multi-device semantics, Node subprocess spawn hygiene) that is itself a failure surface — plus whole Cloud API feature families (message templates, interactive messages, flows, payments, catalogs, quality rating) unexpressed or half-expressed. - Operator/community-reported pain already on record: reaction-status mirror missing (#23899), group mention gating incomplete (#7269), Node-bridge dependency contested (#7274 Neonize pure-Python path). ## Method (three-wave blind analysis + validation) 1. **Wave 1** — 5 blind analysis workers, one per domain shard (S1 core messaging, S2 Cloud API business surface, S3 groups, S4 bridge/backend lifecycle, S5 rich features), each in an isolated worktree at a pinned main. Output: gap catalog (GAP_UNSUPPORTED / GAP_PARTIAL / GAP_CONFLICTED / GAP_DOCS / GAP_BUG_TRACKED) with docs-anchor + repo-file evidence, plus per-domain adapter cluster maps. The S6 decomposition lane produces the graph-before-slice cluster map from the same wave. 2. **Wave 2** — 5 blind cross-check workers, same inputs, forbidden from reading wave-1 output. Agreement between two independent witnesses is the public-confidence bar. 3. **Wave 3** — validation: every agreed gap re-verified at current main + live tracker; issue drafts with evidence and interlock links; existing coverage → interlock, never duplicate. ## Lanes | Lane | Domain | Status | |---|---|---| | S1 | Core messaging: text, media (image/document/audio/video/sticker), reactions, edits, deletes, typing, location/contact sharing | wave analysis | | S2 | Business Cloud API surface: message templates, 24h customer-service window, webhooks, phone-number provisioning, quality rating, rate limits | wave analysis | | S3 | Groups: metadata, mentions, admin ops, invite links, descriptions, per-sender gating (#48394 class), group controls (#7992 class) | wave analysis | | S4 | **Bridge/backend lifecycle**: whatsapp-web.js / Baileys spawn, QR pairing, reconnect/backoff, multi-device semantics, Node subprocess hygiene (windows_detach_popen_kwargs), Neonize pure-Python path (#7274) | wave analysis | | S5 | Rich features: interactive messages (buttons/lists), flows, payments, catalogs, ephemeral, status/broadcast | wave analysis | | S6 | **Decomposition & headroom**: graph-before-slice extraction of adapter.py clusters (backend dispatch, bridge lifecycle, messaging, media, groups, secret + Windows hygiene) — one PR per cluster, seam identity + regression tests, suite green. Core adapter lands far under 2,000 lines: it never has a chance of crossing the ceiling | cluster maps in waves; plan issue follows agreement | ## Deliverables - One issue per confirmed gap (this meta links them all; each issue carries `Campaign: WhatsApp` and interlock links). - Interlock of all pre-existing WhatsApp issues/PRs into lanes (no orphan artifacts). - `whatsapp-dev` skill shipped with Hermes (Cloud API + bridge operations, multi-backend diagnostics) — created during this campaign. - S6 decomposition plan issue + one PR per extraction cluster (adapter.py core shrinks with headroom; seam tests + regression suite per Shard). - Public reconciliation document per cluster/gap: members, evidence, both waves' bases, confidence, verdict. ## Standards (hard) - **Evidence everywhere**: every issue cites the docs anchor + repo `file:line` verified at main. - **Exact numbers**: counts measured, never "about". - **No duplicate issues**: existing coverage → interlock with the exact number. - **One PR per bug class** when fixes ship; suite green; attribution to the author who earned it. - Security/data-loss findings get P1 (this surface is security-sensitive: pairing credentials, phone-number PII); everything else P2/P3. - **No hype**: every capability claim carries a witness receipt before it may appear in public copy. ## Ledger | Issue | Lane | Gap | PR | State | |---|---|---|---|---| | #80094 | S4 | `is_reconnect` cold-respawn bug | #80608 | integration-ready |

signal.title: Cron agents without HERMES_KANBAN_TASK get mandatory kanban_show protocol
signal.text: ## Summary Scheduled cron-agent runs on the Dan profile are receiving the Kanban task execution protocol in system context even when they are not Kanban-dispatched workers and do not have `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` set. The protocol says to call `kanban_show()` first, which returns `task_id is required`; the warning then appears in `recent_dan_errors`, causing the `dan-blockers-slack` cron to report a tooling regression instead of staying silent when `has_blockers=false`. ## Evidence - Collector: `ct-meta/plugins/ct-workflow/skills/dan-mission-coordinator/scripts/dan_blockers_context.py` - Repeated warning shape: `Tool kanban_show returned error ... {"error": "task_id is required (or set HERMES_KANBAN_TASK in the env)"}` - Affected cron: `dan-blockers-slack` on profile `dan`, deliver `slack:C0BDR52KKSL` ## Expected Non-Kanban scheduled cron jobs should not be instructed to run `kanban_show()` as a mandatory first step unless `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` is set, or the Kanban protocol should explicitly exempt cron-triggered runs with no task id. ## Actual The job starts with the Kanban task execution protocol, calls `kanban_show()` with no task id, and records a warning every run. ## Suggested fix Gate the Kanban task execution protocol injection on `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`/worker dispatch context, or make the protocol say cron/scheduled agent jobs without a task id must skip `kanban_show()`.

signal.title: fix(security): redact OAuth JSON fields
signal.text: ## Summary - redact OAuth and key-bearing JSON fields that the central text redactor previously missed - cover snake_case and camelCase forms of client secrets and private keys - preserve unrelated JSON fields unchanged ## Root cause `_SENSITIVE_BODY_KEYS` already classifies `id_token`, `authorization`, `client_secret`, and `private_key` as sensitive, but the separate `_JSON_KEY_NAMES` regex did not include them. As a result, serialized JSON containing opaque values under those keys passed through `redact_sensitive_text()` unchanged. ## Impact Tool output, logs, or transcripts containing serialized OAuth responses or request metadata can now mask these credential values through the existing central redaction path. ## Validation - reproduced all six snake_case/camelCase samples leaking on current `main` - focused smoke: all synthetic values are absent after redaction - focused smoke: unrelated `{"model": "gpt-5"}` JSON remains unchanged - `python -m py_compile agent/redact.py` - `git diff --check`

signal.title: Spoken reply jumps back — reads old reply from several turns ago during hands-free voice conversation (after barge-in)
signal.text: ## Bug Description In hands-free voice conversation (continuous conversation), the spoken reply occasionally **jumps back and reads an old reply from several turns ago** instead of the current response. Observed 5-6 times since yesterday on the latest desktop build. The user's own observation: it tends to happen **after a barge-in / interruption** — as if the previously interrupted speech session is never fully released and resurfaces on a later turn. ## Environment - Hermes Agent `v0.20.5` (2026.8.22) - Windows 11, desktop app - STT: local faster-whisper (`large-v3-turbo`, lang=zh) - TTS: Edge (default), hands-free mode reads every reply (hardcoded in voice-conversation mode) - Wake word: sherpa, custom Chinese wake word, enabled ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start hands-free voice conversation and hold several turns 2. During one turn's spoken reply, interrupt (barge in by speaking, or press stop) 3. Continue to the next turn 4. Occasionally the next reply is spoken **from an old turn's text** (several turns back), not the current one Frequency: intermittent, ~5-6 occurrences over a day of heavy use. Only a manual interruption (speaking over it / stop) cuts the wrong playback. ## Expected Behavior Only the current reply is spoken; interrupted/old speech sessions are fully cleaned up after barge-in. ## Actual Behavior The frontend speaks stale text from an earlier response. The agent side is healthy: `agent.log` shows every `TTS audio saved ... provider: edge` generation corresponds to the current reply (timestamped files, no ordering issue) — the bug is in the desktop playback layer, not the TTS engine. ## Code Pointers (from a quick source read) - `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.ts` - `openLiveSpeech` (~L488): streaming speech session per response; guards with `responseIdRef.current !== responseId`, but a barge-in path can leave the old session/timer around (`feedSpeechSession` interval at L552, cleared only on `session.done`) - `awaitFallbackSpeech` (~L437): whole-text fallback with a 250ms poll loop; the poll is guarded by `responseIdRef` but there is no explicit cancellation on barge-in — a stale poll could later call `playSpeechText(response.text, ...)` with an old response object - `feedSpeechSession` (~L409): appends delta text via `spokenSourceLengthRef`; if an old session is still referenced in `speechSessionRef` after interruption, a new turn can feed into the stale session - `apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-playback.ts` `playSpeechText` (L438): calls `stopVoicePlayback()` first and uses a `sequence` compare (`ownSequence === sequence`) to detect staleness — but the fallback path (`playSpeechDataUrl`) and stream-resolve windows may still race. Hypothesis: after barge-in, the interrupted speech session and its feed timer are not deterministically torn down, so a subsequent turn reuses or replays stale text. ## Related - #91987 Hands-free voice conversation doesn't release microphone after 'stop' — wake word unresponsive until app restart (same voice-mode state-machine family) - #74337 fix(desktop): voice conversation can remain muted after reply playback - #80257 fix(desktop): fix a TOCTOU race in wake-word client-capture start/stop - #85770 fix(wake): stop client-capture wake from arming a deaf listener

signal.title: [Bug] OpenViking plugin uses uid-less viking://user/<segment> URIs that upstream removed in #4196 — will 400 on next OV release
signal.text: ## Bug Description The OpenViking memory plugin still emits **uid-less `viking://user/<segment>` URIs**, a spelling that upstream OpenViking **removed in commit #4196** (`feat(uri)!: remove uid-less current-user shorthand in favor of viking://~`, merged 2026-08-21 into main). Per the upstream BREAKING CHANGE note, requests using that spelling now fail with **HTTP 400** (`NamespaceShapeError`) — the server no longer expands `viking://user/<reserved-segment>` to the current user's space. Affected hardcoded URIs in `plugins/memory/openviking/__init__.py`: - L96 `_PROFILE_URI = "viking://user/memories/profile.md"` - L97 `_PREFERENCES_URI = "viking://user/memories/preferences"` - L98 `_ENTITIES_URI = "viking://user/memories/entities"` - L4782 `_build_memory_uri()` → `viking://user/peers/{agent}/memories/{subdir}/mem_{slug}.md` - L576 tool description example string (`viking://user/memories/`) - README.md references to `viking://user/peers/...` All of these flow through the REST API (`/api/v1/content/read`, `/api/v1/content/write`). On the OpenViking server every content endpoint validates via `validate_request_viking_uri` → `resolve_request_uri` → `resolve_current_user_uri`, which **rejects** `viking://user/<segment>` when the segment is a reserved name (`memories`, `resources`, `skills`, `peers`, `privacy`, `sessions`) and differs from the caller's user_id. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run an OpenViking server built from current main (contains #4196), or wait for the next release after 0.4.16. 2. Start Hermes with the OpenViking memory provider (trusted mode, no API key; local ovcli config with `actor_peer_id: hermes`). 3. Any session start or memory write triggers the plugin's REST calls with the old URI spelling. ## Expected Behavior - Session-start profile/preferences/entities reads succeed. - `on_memory_write` mirroring writes succeed. - Works with the current OpenViking release AND future releases. ## Actual Behavior - All requests using `viking://user/memories/...` / `viking://user/peers/...` return 400 from the server → profile/preferences/entities never reach the model context, and memory mirroring silently fails. - Today it does not crash only because the locally installed server is 0.4.15 (released before #4196). PyPI 0.4.16 (2026-08-21) also predates #4196, so it still accepts the old spelling — but the next OpenViking release will break the plugin. ## Root Cause Analysis OpenViking introduced `viking://~` as the unambiguous current-user home alias in #4167 (merged 2026-08-20, included in the 0.4.16 release), then removed the ambiguous uid-less shorthand in #4196 (merged 2026-08-21, main only). Upstream migrated all first-party clients (vikingbot, langchain, openclaw, dsh, pi plugin, etc.) to `viking://~/...` in the same PR. The Hermes plugin is a third-party client that was not migrated. ## Proposed Fix Replace the uid-less spellings with the `viking://~` home alias in `plugins/memory/openviking/__init__.py` (and README): - `viking://~/memories/profile.md` - `viking://~/memories/preferences` - `viking://~/memories/entities` - `viking://~/peers/{agent}/memories/{subdir}/mem_{slug}.md` Notes: - `viking://~` requires OpenViking server >= 0.4.16 (alias landed in #4167). Older servers (0.4.15) will not understand it — but they still accept the old spelling, so the change is safe once the server is on 0.4.16+. - In trusted mode the plugin's identity is `account=default, user=default, actor_peer=hermes`, so `~` expands to `viking://user/default/...` — identical to the current on-disk layout (`viking/default/user/default/memories/profile.md`), so no data migration is needed. - The `viking://user/peers/{agent}/...` write path in `_build_memory_uri()` is affected too (peers is also a reserved segment) — this one is the most impactful because it is the memory-mirroring write path.

signal.title: [Bug]: delegation live transcripts resolve HERMES_HOME after a thread hop and can write to another profile
signal.text: ### Bug description In a multi-profile process, `delegate_task` live-transcript files can be written under a different profile from the session that initiated the delegation. Observed on Hermes Agent **v0.19.1 (v2026.7.30)**: one session running as profile `generic-core` produced delegation transcripts under both: ```text /root/.hermes/profiles/generic-core/cache/delegation/live/ /root/.hermes/profiles/thindi/cache/delegation/live/ ``` The destination varied with concurrent worker timing. The relevant code is unchanged in v0.20.5 (`v2026.8.19`) and current `main` (`b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff` as checked on 2026-08-22). ### Expected behavior Every delegation artifact created by a session should be rooted under that session's resolved profile home, regardless of thread scheduling or concurrent sessions on other profiles. ### Actual behavior `tools/delegation_live_log.py:61-65` resolves the root implicitly: ```python def live_transcript_root() -> Path: """Root directory for live transcripts (profile-safe, never ~/.hermes).""" from hermes_constants import get_hermes_dir return get_hermes_dir("cache/delegation", "delegation_cache") / "live" ``` `get_hermes_dir()` therefore uses ambient `get_hermes_home()` state. If the call runs after a raw `threading.Thread` boundary, the originating `_HERMES_HOME_OVERRIDE` value is absent because `ContextVar` values do not automatically propagate to new threads. Resolution falls through to process-wide `HERMES_HOME` or the default home. In a multi-profile WebUI process, process-wide `HERMES_HOME` is also unsuitable as a session identity because concurrent workers temporarily change it for different profiles. ### Deterministic reproduction This reproduces without a model call and writes only under a temporary directory: ```python import os import tempfile import threading from pathlib import Path from hermes_constants import ( reset_hermes_home_override, set_hermes_home_override, ) from tools.delegation_live_log import create_live_transcripts with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td: td = Path(td) process_home = td / "process-default-thindi" session_home = td / "session-generic-core" process_home.mkdir() session_home.mkdir() old = os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME") os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(process_home) token = set_hermes_home_override(session_home) out = {} try: def worker(): _id, _writers, paths = create_live_transcripts( [{"goal": "profile path repro"}] ) out["path"] = paths[0] thread = threading.Thread(target=worker) thread.start() thread.join() finally: reset_hermes_home_override(token) if old is None: os.environ.pop("HERMES_HOME", None) else: os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = old actual = Path(out["path"]) expected_root = session_home / "cache/delegation/live" wrong_root = process_home / "cache/delegation/live" print("actual_path=", actual) print("expected_under_session=", actual.is_relative_to(expected_root)) print("actual_under_process_default=", actual.is_relative_to(wrong_root)) ``` Observed output on v0.19.1: ```text actual_path= /tmp/.../process-default-thindi/cache/delegation/live/deleg_.../task-0.log expected_under_session= False actual_under_process_default= True ``` A minimal `ContextVar` control also confirms the boundary behavior: ```text plain threading.Thread: process/default value copy_context().run(thread target): session/profile value ``` ### Root cause `hermes_constants.py` defines `_HERMES_HOME_OVERRIDE` as a `ContextVar` and `get_hermes_home()` correctly consults it first. The missing invariant is that profile identity is not explicitly carried across every concurrency boundary before profile-scoped paths are resolved. `get_hermes_dir()` already documents the intended contract: ```text home: Optional explicit Hermes home. Profile-aware callers that manage more than one home in the same process use this instead of temporarily mutating the process or context-local HERMES_HOME. ``` However, `delegation_live_log.live_transcript_root()` does not pass `home=`. The delegation fan-out itself uses `contextvars.copy_context()` for its child executor tasks, but that is too late to repair a profile context already lost when the parent agent turn entered through an earlier raw thread boundary. It also does not make process-global `os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]` safe for concurrent profiles. ### Suggested fix Prefer explicit profile-home threading for profile-scoped delegation artifacts: 1. Resolve the delegation home from stable parent-owned state at `delegate_task` entry. On current Hermes, the parent's profile-specific `SessionDB.db_path.parent` is one available source; an explicit `profile_home` field on the agent would be cleaner. 2. Add a `home: Path | None` parameter to `live_transcript_root()` / `create_live_transcripts()`. 3. Call: ```python get_hermes_dir( "cache/delegation", "delegation_cache", home=resolved_profile_home, ) ``` 4. Add a regression test that creates a session-home override, crosses a raw thread boundary with a different process `HERMES_HOME`, and asserts every transcript/manifest path stays under the session home. Capturing `contextvars.copy_context()` at every raw thread spawn is useful defense in depth, especially in WebUI/desktop entry points, but explicit `home=` is the stronger storage-boundary fix because it does not depend on ambient context surviving future executor/thread refactors. ### Impact - Cross-profile leakage of operational transcripts, goals, tool arguments/results, and metadata. - Missing live logs in the initiating profile and misleading paths returned to the parent. - Non-deterministic behavior under concurrent profile activity. - Profile deletion/retention can affect artifacts owned by another profile. The transcript redactor reduces credential exposure, but writing a profile's operational data into another profile remains an isolation violation. ### Related upstream work - #18594 — broader wrong-profile fallback class. - #88715 — canonical profile identity must survive async/thread boundaries. - #77015 — live-transcript path visibility for Docker/remote backends; different root cause. - #81267 / merged PR #86668 — v0.19.1 delegated children borrowed the parent's `SessionDB`; fixed after v0.19.1 with child-owned connections at the parent's `db_path`. - #91610 / PR #91631 — newer shared launch-`SessionDB` ownership variant causing `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'execute'`; separate from this live-log path defect. ### Environment - Hermes Agent: v0.19.1 (`v2026.7.30`) - Install method: git / Hermes WebUI combined runtime - OS: Linux - Python: 3.12.13 - Multi-profile process: `generic-core` and `thindi` 🤖 This was written by an AI coding agent

signal.title: fix(copilot): preserve signed thinking across tool results
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? It preserves Claude signed-thinking blocks when the Anthropic Messages adapter is pointed at GitHub Copilot's `/v1/messages` relay. The adapter currently treats every non-Anthropic host except Nous Portal as signature-blind and strips all thinking blocks. Copilot implements Claude's signed-thinking contract end to end: a response can contain `thinking + signature + tool_use`, and the next request must replay that assistant block unchanged together with the tool result. Stripping the block loses reasoning continuity and violates the endpoint's replay contract. This change classifies Copilot hosts with hostname-safe matching and lets the latest assistant turn follow the native signed-thinking replay path. Generic third-party proxies keep the existing stripping behavior. ## Related Issue Related to #57625. That PR enables the default catalog route to `/v1/messages`; this PR fixes the adapter-level replay behavior required once that route is used. It does not duplicate the routing or Bearer-auth changes. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Add hostname-safe detection for Copilot's Anthropic Messages relay. - Exempt that relay from generic third-party thinking-block stripping. - Preserve the exact `thinking`, `text`, `tool_use` order and signature bytes. - Add a generic-proxy control proving other third-party behavior is unchanged. - Add path/suffix lookalikes proving host detection cannot be triggered by string containment. ## How to Test 1. Run `python -m pytest tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py -q`. 2. Before the implementation change, the Copilot replay test fails with `['text', 'tool_use']`; after the change it passes with `['thinking', 'text', 'tool_use']`. 3. Run `ruff check agent/anthropic_adapter.py tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py`. Live protocol validation used a synthetic tool call: - response 1 returned `thinking + signature + tool_use`; - request 2 replayed the exact signed block before the tool result; - response 2 returned new thinking plus a final answer; - a deliberately altered signature was rejected with HTTP 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block`. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits - [x] I searched existing PRs and documented the relationship to #57625 - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant behavior is documented in the adapter docstring; no user documentation change is needed - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` changes are N/A - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` changes are N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact; the change uses the existing URL helper and has no OS-specific behavior - [x] Tool description/schema changes are N/A ## Verification - `tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py`: 97 passed, 1 skipped - Neighboring Anthropic reasoning/signature selection: 130 passed, 1 skipped - Ruff: all checks passed - Mutation gate: removing the relay exemption fails only the Copilot replay assertion while the host-safety and generic-proxy controls remain green

signal.title: fix(agent): detect tool-call argument and result jitter
signal.text: ## Summary Follow-up to #90338 and the scoped request in #85323. The merged `observe_identical_call()` guard catches exact repeats, but explicit no-progress representations could still mint a fresh observation: 1. A declarative `todo` call can jitter `merge: true` / `false` while re-asserting the same ordered task state. 2. `read_file` and `skill_view` can replace a full result with an explicit unchanged envelope (`status: "unchanged"`, `dedup: true`, `content_returned: false`). The envelope hashes differently even though it certifies that the underlying result did not change. This change: - gives the observational stall guard a narrowly normalized signature for `todo`, ignoring only `merge`; - keeps todo item order significant because it defines priority; - carries the consecutive streak through a validated unchanged/dedup envelope, scoped to the tools that actually emit that contract (`read_file`, `skill_view`); - anchors the streak on its original result hash, so a loop alternating full payload ↔ dedup stub still reaches the threshold while a genuinely changed result resets it; - resets normally for lookalike payloads missing the full dedup contract; - leaves all other tools, failure/no-progress signatures, and poller exemptions unchanged. ## Test plan - [x] Canonical runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/agent/test_stall_guards.py tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py tests/tools/test_skill_view_dedup.py` — 43 passed, 0 failed - [x] `ruff check agent/tool_guardrails.py tests/agent/test_stall_guards.py` - [x] Mutation check: removing todo signature normalization fails the todo jitter regression - [x] Mutation check: removing explicit unchanged-result handling fails the result-jitter regression - [x] Independent adversarial review of the state machine; findings (full↔stub alternation reset, unscoped envelope contract) fixed in `8d74772` with regression tests - [x] Broader file-tool suite attempted: 84 passed, 2 skipped, 2 unrelated macOS `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp` mock-path failures - [x] Remote branch head verified after push Closes the additive arg/result-jitter gap identified in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/85323#issuecomment-5350440406

signal.title: fix(approvals): log a birth record when a gateway approval prompt is raised
signal.text: ## Problem When a dangerous-command approval prompt is raised in a gateway session (desktop/TUI or a chat platform), the request is emitted over the session transport. If that transport is dead at emit time — e.g. the client disconnected moments earlier during a long turn — three things go wrong (#91980): 1. **No birth record.** The BLOCKED outcome lands in logs ~300s later, but nothing records that a prompt was ever raised. 2. **No delivery check.** The notify callback writes into the session transport; a write onto a closed transport drops silently, and the agent thread blocks anyway. 3. Every delivery failure therefore looks identical to user silence — the operator's only recovery is noticing the BLOCKED line in a log file after the fact. ## Root cause `_await_gateway_decision` (`tools/approval.py`) enqueues the prompt, fires the plugin hooks, calls the notify callback, and blocks — with no log line at raise time. The existing approval-gate log artifacts are all outcome-level (hardline blocks, notify exceptions, the tool-facing BLOCKED message), so a prompt that was raised but never delivered leaves zero trace. ## Change Add one WARNING-level birth record in `_await_gateway_decision`, fired right before the notify callback: ``` Approval prompt raised: session=<key> pattern=<pattern_key> surface=<surface> ``` - One seam covers **every** gateway approval surface: `_await_gateway_decision` is shared by the terminal command guard, the execute_code guard, protected-file writes (`tools/file_tools.py`), the action guard, and elicitation consent. - Field set matches the issue's suggested direction 1 (session key / pattern key / surface; the timestamp comes from the logging formatter). The raw command is deliberately kept out — the approval payload carries the *un-redacted* command, and the birth record only needs identity, not content. - Coalesced followers join the leader's prompt and don't re-log (one prompt, one birth record), matching the existing coalescing semantics. This is the cheapest of the issue's three suggested directions and makes incidents diagnosable after the fact. Direction 2 (delivery acknowledgement / fail-fast) and direction 3 (fallback surface) change wait semantics and are left as separate decisions for maintainers. ## Tests New `tests/tools/test_approval_birth_log.py`: - the raise-time WARNING contains session / pattern / surface - the birth record omits the raw command (redaction contract) ## Verification - `pytest tests/tools/test_approval_birth_log.py` — 2 passed - `pytest tests/tools/test_approval.py tests/tools/test_approval_interrupt.py tests/tools/test_command_guards.py` — 132 passed; the single failure (`TestDetectDangerousRm::test_nonrecursive_verification_artifact_cleanup_is_not_dangerous`) fails identically on a clean `main` checkout on this macOS host (environment-sensitive `/tmp` resolution) and is unrelated to this change. ## Notes Refs #91980 — implements direction 1 (birth logging) from the issue's suggested list; directions 2 and 3 remain open as larger design decisions.

signal.title: fix(update): refuse ZIP fallback when the working tree is dirty
signal.text: ## Summary - On Windows, `hermes update` can fall back to a ZIP overlay that extracts over the working tree and then moves HEAD. Uncommitted local patches were overwritten with no warning, `git status` went clean, and the update reported success. - The git path already aborts when it cannot stash ("Commit, stash, or clean up your local changes"). Fixes #91962 ## Test plan - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_zip_dirty_tree.py` — dirty / untracked / status-failed trees abort; clean tree and non-git roots are allowed; overlay is refused before `urlretrieve` - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_zip_two_phase.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_zip_symlink_reject.py` — existing ZIP path tests still pass - [ ] On Windows with a dirty checkout, force the ZIP path (`hermes update` after git I/O breakage) and confirm it prints `ZIP fallback refused` and leaves local edits intact

signal.title: Hands-free voice conversation doesn't release microphone after 'stop' — wake word unresponsive until app restart
signal.text: ## Bug Description After ending a hands-free voice conversation (continuous conversation) by saying "stop", the microphone capture is not released properly. The wake word becomes unresponsive afterwards — saying it does nothing until the desktop app is fully restarted. ## Environment - Hermes Agent `v0.20.5` (2026.8.22) - Windows 11, desktop app - STT: local faster-whisper (`large-v3-turbo`, lang=zh) - Wake word: sherpa, custom Chinese wake word (single user phrase), enabled - Microphone: external USB microphone (MME host API) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable wake word + hands-free voice conversation 2. Start a hands-free conversation and speak 3. Say "stop" to end the recording/conversation 4. Try the wake word again — nothing happens (no wake detection; mic appears held/not released) ## Expected Behavior After the conversation ends, the mic capture stream is released and the wake-word detector resumes listening normally. ## Actual Behavior The wake-word detector fails to resume. Log evidence: - `logs/gui.log`: `wake.resume: detector resumed=False` after the conversation ends (normally `resumed=True` in healthy operation) - `logs/errors.log`: continuous `wake word: mic delivers only silence (peak<=10 for 10s); ... from the default input device (MME)` warnings, repeating every ~10s for 10+ minutes - `logs/desktop.log`: repeated `AudioContext encountered an error from the audio device or the WebAudio renderer` Only a full app restart releases the microphone and restores wake-word detection. ## Related - #74337 fix(desktop): voice conversation can remain muted after reply playback - #84316 Desktop app: getUserMedia fails with 'Microphone already in use' on Windows 11 - #74996 fix: wake word mic-busy retry with actionable error messages - #85770 fix(wake): stop client-capture wake from arming a deaf listener

signal.title: fix(process): persist completion-consumed markers durably across processes
signal.text: ## Problem Background-process completion tracking ("was this completion already consumed / delivered?") is kept **in memory only** (`ProcessRegistry._completion_consumed`). After an agent or gateway restart, the ledger is empty, so a completion notification for a long-running background process can be delivered **a second time** to the session — duplicated wake messages, duplicated user-visible noise. ## Fix Persist consumption durably, scoped to the Hermes home directory: - markers live under `<hermes_home>/processes-consumed/<process_id>.consumed`; - `_mark_completion_consumed()` writes the marker file in addition to the in-memory set (best-effort: file failures never break the in-memory path); - `is_completion_consumed()` checks both memory and the durable marker, so a **fresh** `ProcessRegistry` instance (new process, post-restart) still recognises already-consumed completions; - marker filenames are validated (unsafe ids skip file ops entirely — no path traversal); - a TTL sweep (7 days) removes stale markers so the directory cannot grow unboundedly. No schema changes, no new dependencies; the durable layer degrades gracefully to today's in-memory behavior if the filesystem is unavailable. ## Tests `tests/tools/test_process_registry.py` — new `TestConsumedMarkers` class (6 tests): - marking writes a durable marker file; - a **second, fresh** `ProcessRegistry` instance sees the completion as consumed (the restart scenario); - absent marker ⇒ not consumed; - unsafe session ids never touch the filesystem; - TTL sweep removes only stale markers; - `wait()` marks completion durably. ``` python -m pytest tests/tools/test_process_registry.py -q # 58 passed ``` ## Relation to other work Independent of, but complementary to, #76144 (background spawn cwd re-pin). Whichever lands second should rebase trivially over the other (adjacent test-file context only). ## Risk Low: additive persistence with in-memory fallback; no behavior change within a single process lifetime; cross-process dedup only *reduces* duplicate notifications.

signal.title: fix(desktop): prevent remote config overwrite & preserve basic auth credentials (#88913)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #88913 where Hermes Desktop, when connected to an authenticated remote backend, autosaved a stale local/default config snapshot over the remote server's `config.yaml` upon browsing or saving Settings. ### Root Cause 1. **Stale Cache Lock-In**: React Query cached the local config record under `['hermes-config-record']`. On gateway connection swap, components like `ConfigSettings` mounted with the stale local config before background refetch finished, setting `configSeeded.current = true` and ignoring subsequent remote fetches. 2. **Full Snapshot Clobbering**: Desktop sent a full `HermesConfigRecord` snapshot in `PUT /api/config`. The server's `_deep_merge` overwrote remote `config.yaml` fields with Desktop's un-edited local defaults. 3. **Basic Auth Erasure**: Generic serialization sent empty strings `""` for `dashboard.basic_auth`, erasing basic auth credentials on the remote backend. ### Fix - **Revision / ETag Tracking**: `GET /api/config` attaches a 16-character SHA-256 `_revision` token. `PUT /api/config` checks `expected_revision` and returns **HTTP 409 Conflict** on stale writes. - **Security Boundary Shield**: Added `_protect_sensitive_config_fields` in `web_server.py` to prevent empty string overwrites of `dashboard.basic_auth` credentials. - **Desktop Cache Purging**: Added `resetHermesConfigCache()` called during `wipeSessionListsForGatewaySwitch()` to clear query caches on connection re-home. - **Re-seeding**: Draft re-synchronizes when a fresh remote `_revision` lands if `saveVersion === 0`. ### Verification & Stress Benchmarks - **Unit Tests**: Added `test_remote_config_protection.py` (4 passed). - **Web Server Suite**: 159 tests passed. - **Stress Load Benchmark**: `test_config_endpoint_stress.py` demonstrated **140.8 req/sec** read throughput (69.17 ms avg latency) and 100% CAS safety (20 atomic writes, 80 revision conflict 409 rejections, 0 errors). Closes #88913 ## Infographic :

No historical green from `eaf71c8...`, `825d9c1...`, or any predecessor head is merge authority for `831b7fc...`. ## Surviving architecture contract The intended class-level seam remains valid: - transport credential ownership, runtime/profile ownership, and physical persistence ownership are distinct axes; - a durable carrier may select the expected transport claimant but cannot self-certify current credential custody; - current transport authority must be represented by a non-secret claim identity plus adapter generation and a `unique | ambiguous | unavailable` verdict; - ambiguous, unavailable, owner-mismatched, or stale-generation carriers fail closed before adapter-local or runner stateful use; - intentional shared-credential routing remains valid when one unique current transport owner serves multiple runtime profiles; - per-profile physical `state.db` remains repository truth from merged #88734; and - #89860 remains authoritative for adapter owner stamping/session-key behavior and contributor provenance. ## Missing executable transition The current workflow attempts to materialize the claimant/generation repair, inject the production `BasePlatformAdapter.handle_message` gate, run the focused routing/claim suites, amend the generated object, and upload an exact product tree against current main `b6bcb3e791c673e63974029bbab40cc9326803ff`. That materializer did **not** produce a successful artifact on the live head. Therefore the claimant/generation repair is not yet a branch-tree fact and is not verified as a merge candidate. ## Closure gate Before this PR can leave draft: 1. make the claimant-generation materialization/build path succeed or publish the equivalent reviewed production diff directly; 2. remove temporary carrier/materializer machinery from the final product diff; 3. prove duplicate current claim rejection, stale generation after credential rotation, unique restart recovery, intentional shared-credential routing, and production ingress gating; 4. attach the real hash-pinned migration drill; 5. compose onto exact current `main`; and 6. obtain fresh exact-head CI/Docker/Nix with zero unresolved review threads. signal.title: fix(profiles): preserve safe symlinks on archive import
signal.text: ## Summary - preserve profile-confined relative symlinks when importing profile archives - validate every member and link target before writing, then create symlinks after regular members - continue rejecting hardlinks, absolute/drive-qualified targets, root escapes, and duplicate or case-colliding member paths ## Problem `export_profile()` intentionally stages profiles with `symlinks=True`, but `_safe_extract_profile_archive()` rejected every symlink member. A profile archive produced by Hermes could therefore fail to import when it contained a valid relative symlink. ## Security model Symlink targets are normalized lexically relative to the link parent and must remain under the archive's single profile root. Regular files and directories are extracted first, so archive order cannot turn a later file write into symlink traversal. Hardlinks and other special member types remain unsupported. Duplicate normalized paths, including case-only collisions that alias on Windows, are rejected before extraction. ## Verification - WSL Ubuntu: `163 passed` for `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` - Windows targeted import cases: `8 passed, 1 skipped` (normal symlink creation skipped only when the host lacks the optional privilege) - `ruff check hermes_cli/profiles.py tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` - `git diff --check` Duplicate searches for `profile import symlink`, `profile archive symlink`, and `Unsupported archive member type` found no other open fix PR. Related context: #58394 established that profile export must preserve symlinks.

signal.title: fix(gateway): don't freeze inbound on Telegram flood sleep during boot
signal.text: ## Summary - Telegram `send()` slept the server `retry_after` with no ceiling, so a 97-minute flood penalty pinned the send coroutine. - That send ran on the gateway boot path *before* the startup-restore gate opened, so inbound on every platform was queued and never processed. Restarting re-entered the same sleep. - Cap long flood waits the same way the edit path already does (fail closed above 5s), and bound boot-path sends so the inbound gate still opens on schedule. `resume_pending` is cleared before redelivery send so a timed-out send cannot also replay the turn. Fixes #91969 ## Test plan - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_telegram_send_path_health.py` — long `retry_after` fails closed with no sleep; short waits still retry inline - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_restart_resume_pending.py` — hung boot-path send releases the inbound gate; fast path still runs notification + redelivery - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_delivery_ledger.py` — `resume_pending` is cleared before a hanging redelivery send - [ ] Reproduce: trip Telegram flood control, restart the gateway, send a message on webhook/api_server while Telegram is still penalized — inbound should be answered instead of staying queued
